  2. Subagentes

  La sesión principal hace de orquestador y sigue FLOW.md. En Claude Code un
  subagente no puede lanzar otros subagentes, así que la coordinación queda en
  la sesión principal.

  Agente: spec-writer
  Responsabilidad: Convierte la US en spec verificable: detecta huecos, numera
    BR/AC y abre preguntas para el humano
  Herramientas: Read, Grep, Glob, Write (solo specs/)
  Entrada → Salida: story.md → spec.md, tasks.md
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Agente: architect
  Responsabilidad: Detecta decisiones, escribe ADRs con alternativas reales y
    valida que la spec no choque con ADRs vigentes
  Herramientas: Read, Grep, Glob, Write (solo adr/), WebFetch (docs oficiales)
  Entrada → Salida: spec.md → adr/NNNN-*.md (Proposed)
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Agente: test-engineer
  Responsabilidad: Escribe los tests desde la spec, antes del código (unit +
    e2e), sin leer la implementación primero
  Herramientas: Read, Write, Edit, Bash (test runners)
  Entrada → Salida: spec.md → *.spec.ts, e2e/*.spec.ts
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Agente: strapi-developer
  Responsabilidad: Content types, seed CO/CL, permisos del rol público,
    bootstrap
  Herramientas: Read, Write, Edit, Bash (dentro de backend/)
  Entrada → Salida: spec + ADR + tasks → backend/**
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Agente: angular-developer
  Responsabilidad: Wizard, formulario dinámico, estado con signals, a11y y
    responsive
  Herramientas: Read, Write, Edit, Bash (dentro de frontend/)
  Entrada → Salida: spec + ADR + tasks + tests rojos → frontend/**
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Agente: code-reviewer
  Responsabilidad: Revisión independiente contra la spec, la checklist y los
    ADRs. No edita código
  Herramientas: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash (solo lint/test/build), Write (solo
    reviews/)
  Entrada → Salida: diff + spec → reviews/US-0X-review-RN.md

  El tester está separado de los desarrolladores a propósito: si quien
  implementa escribe sus propios tests, tiende a validar lo que hizo y no lo que
  pide la spec.

  4. Flujo y puntos de control humanos

  H0 Intake (humano, sin IA) → 1 Spec → [HC1] → 2 ADRs → [HC2] → 3 Tests rojos
  → 4 Implementación → 5 Gate automático → 6 Review → 7 Fixes → [HC3 PR] → Ready
  for QA

  Punto de control: HC1 Spec
  Qué revisas: spec.md
  Apruebas si…: Cada AC tiene ID y es verificable, las preguntas abiertas
    están resueltas por ti, el fuera de alcance es explícito y no hay
    contradicción con ADRs
  Si rechazas…: Anotas el motivo en la sección Review log de la spec; el
    spec-writer reescribe y queda la versión anterior en git
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Punto de control: HC2 ADR
  Qué revisas: adr/*.md
  Apruebas si…: Hay ≥2 alternativas reales, consecutivas y justificación; el
    estado pasa a Accepted solo si tú lo cambias
  Si rechazas…: Eliges otra alternativa o pasa a Rejected (se conserva); el
    architect reescribe
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Punto de control: Gate auto (sin humano)
  Qué revisas: lint, typecheck, unit, e2e, build, smoke de docker compose
  Apruebas si…: Todo verde
  Si rechazas…: Vuelve al desarrollador; tras 3 vueltas fallidas, escala al
    humano
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Punto de control: HC3 PR
  Qué revisas: PR + review report + QA manual (CO y CL, solo teclado, móvil)
  Apruebas si…: 0 hallazgos blocker/major abiertos, matriz de trazabilidad
    completa, todos los AC verificados a mano
  Si rechazas…: Comentas en el PR y vuelve al paso 4; el merge lo haces tú

  Lo que no hace la IA: el intake de la US, aceptar ADRs, el merge, la prueba
  manual de teclado y a11y, la elección de skills externas y cualquier manejo de
  secretos.

  5. Trazabilidad

  - IDs: US-01 · US-01-BR-03 (regla) · US-01-AC-02 (escenario) · US-01-Q-01
    (hueco o pregunta) · US-01-T-04 (tarea) · ADR-0001 · US-01-R1-F03 (review
    ronda 1, hallazgo 3).
  - Rama: feat/us-01-dynamic-form.
  - Commit: Conventional Commits con trailers, por ejemplo feat(form): …, luego
    Refs: US-01-AC-02, ADR-0001, y en los fixes Resolves: US-01-R1-F03.
  - Tests: describe('US-01-AC-02 field validation', …).
  - Review: cada hallazgo tiene una tabla con el SHA del commit que lo resolvió
    y su estado.
  - PR: la plantilla incluye la matriz AC → archivos → test → estado.
    scripts/trace.sh US-01 la genera con grep, sin IA, para comprobar que nadie
    la inventó.

  6. Cómo se retoma entre sesiones

  - specs/US-0X/tasks.md: tareas con estado, el punto de control actual,
    bloqueos y una línea "Next action". CLAUDE.md obliga a actualizarlo al
    cerrar cada paso.
  - Al iniciar una sesión: leer CLAUDE.md → tasks.md de la HU activa → continuar
    desde "Next action". Todo el estado vive en el repo, sin memoria externa.
  - Logs: al cerrar cada sesión se copia el JSONL crudo de Claude Code y el
    /export a logs/sessions/AAAA-MM-DD-<id>.*, sin editar. Antes del commit, un
    escaneo de secretos (gitleaks o grep); si encuentra algo, no se commitea y
    se avisa.

  2. Las 2 skills nuevas (test-from-spec, session-handoff): ¿entran?

  Quedo esperando tu aprobación explícita (o tus cambios) antes de crear

⏺ Evaluación de angular-developer: ADOPTAR CON AJUSTES

  La dejé registrada en docs/skills/third-party-evaluation.md, todavía sin
  commit. No instalé nada.

  Datos clave
  - Commit evaluado: 97c663a (2026-11-20). El repo es un espejo que se genera
    desde angular/angular (commit 8b15295) y se sincroniza varias veces al día.
    Está activo, no deprecado.
  - Autor: Google LLC. Licencia: MIT, pero solo aparece declarada en el
    frontmatter. El repo espejo no tiene archivo LICENSE, así que en
    THIRD_PARTY.md hay que dejar el aviso de copyright apuntando al MIT de
    angular/angular.
  - Seguridad: solo contiene Markdown; no hay scripts, hooks ni Unicode oculto.
    Los únicos dominios externos son angular.dev, api.example.com y localhost.
    Lo que sí descarga cosas son los npx que sugiere (ng new con @latest y el
    MCP server de Angular CLI).
  - Riesgo de cadena de suministro: npx skills add instala lo que haya en HEAD,
    no el commit que evalué. Por eso propongo hacer un diff contra 97c663a
    después de instalar.

  Compatibilidad
  - Cumple con Angular 22 (la última estable es la 22.3.0), standalone, signals,
    @if/@for, Vitest zoneless y sin NgModules.
  - Playwright: la skill es neutral. Sugiere un schematic comunitario que no
    usaremos.
  - A11y por teclado: solo la cubre en parte (widgets ARIA). El foco del wizard
    y los errores accesibles los sigue cubriendo nuestro review-checklist.

  Choques con nuestras reglas (todos se resuelven en CLAUDE.md, sin tocar los 
  archivos de la skill)
  - C1: signal-forms.md dice que todo formulario debe ser Signal Forms, y eso
    decidiría el ADR antes que nosotros. Se resuelve con una precedencia:
    CLAUDE.md > ADRs aceptados > skills propias > skills de terceros.
  - C2: hace ng new sin fijar versión. Se resuelve fijando la versión del CLI.
  - C3: propone configurar un MCP server. No se usa, porque nada de herramientas
    externas.
  - C5: su convención de nombres es ambigua. La decidimos explícitamente en
    CLAUDE.md.

  Qué aporta que no tengamos: la API de Signal Forms al día, con su tabla de
  errores comunes. Es justo donde un modelo más fácilmente inventa APIs. También
  aporta testing zoneless con Vitest, httpResource para estados de carga y
  error, y configuración en tiempo de ejecución para servir CO y CL con un mismo
  build.

  Signal Forms frente a Reactive Forms (para el ADR): la skill se contradice. Un
  archivo dice "v21+ / MUST" y el otro "estable en v22+ / prefer". Lo comprobé
  en la fuente:
  - Signal Forms pasó a API pública en la 22.0.0 (2026-06-03, commit

  ---

  **1. Subagent frontmatter (.claude/agents/*.md)**
  Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents.md
  Only `name` and `description` are required. Multi-word fields are camelCase.
  Unknown fields are ignored without an error.
  - `name` (required): max 256 chars; no `:` (reserved for plugin scope);
  shouldn't start with `-`.
  - `description` (required): when Claude should delegate.
  - `tools`: comma string (`tools: Read, Grep, Bash`) or YAML list. Omit to
  inherit. If nothing resolves, the subagent usually fails to launch.
  - `disallowedTools`: same format; removes tools from the inherited or listed
  set.
  - `model`: `sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`, `fable`, a full model ID (example given:
  `claude-opus-5-5`), or `inherit`.
  - `permissionMode`: `default`, `acceptEdits`, `auto`, `dontAsk`,
  `bypassPermissions`, `plan`, `manual` (alias of default). Ignored for plugin
  subagents. If the parent is in `bypassPermissions`, `acceptEdits`, or auto
  mode, the parent's mode wins and this field is ignored.
  - `maxTurns`, `autoCompactWindow` (>= 100000, needs v2.1.296+), `background`,
  `omitClaudeMd` (needs v2.1.271+), `effort` (low/medium/high/xhigh/max),
  `isolation: worktree`, `color` (red, blue, green, yellow, purple, orange,
  pink, cyan), `initialPrompt` (ignored for plugin subagents), `experimental`
  (map with `cacheTtl: 5m|1h`, needs v2.1.248+).
  - `memory`: `user`, `project`, or `local`.
  - `mcpServers`: server name strings or inline definitions; ignored for plugin
  subagents.
  - `hooks`: lifecycle hooks scoped to the subagent; ignored for plugin
  subagents (see Q2).
  - `skills`: list of skill names to preload. The full skill content is injected
  at startup, up to 32 distinct names. It controls preloading only, not access:
  without it, the subagent can still discover and invoke skills via the Skill
  tool. To block skill invocation, omit `Skill` from `tools` or add it to
  `disallowedTools`. Skills with `disable-model-invocation: true` cannot be
  preloaded. Missing skills are skipped with a debug-log warning.

  **2. Restricting Write/Edit paths for a subagent**
  Sources: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents.md,
  https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions.md,
  https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md
  - No frontmatter field for a path allowlist is documented. Subagents inherit
  the parent's permission rules (the docs state this for built-in subagents, and
  the Bash deny example says the rule "applies to the main conversation and to
  subagents").
  - Block writes entirely: `disallowedTools: Write, Edit`.
  - Path-scoped enforcement: use a frontmatter PreToolUse hook. Permissions docs
  confirm `file_path` is the parameter for Read, Edit, and Write. A hook can
  deny; it cannot override a deny rule. Example:

  ```yaml
  ---
  name: spec-writer
  description: Writes specs under specs/ only
  tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Write, Edit, Bash
  hooks:
    PreToolUse:
      - matcher: "Write|Edit"
        hooks:
          - type: command
            command: "\"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\"/.claude/hooks/only-specs.sh"
  ---
  ```
  `only-specs.sh` reads `.tool_input.file_path` from stdin JSON (via jq), and
  exits 2 with a message on stderr if the path is not under `specs/`. Use
  `realpath`-style normalization in the script so `../` cannot escape.
  - Project-level agent frontmatter hooks run only after the workspace trust
  dialog is accepted. Otherwise they are skipped with a debug-log error.
  - Documented caveat: the `permissionMode` field does not guarantee protection,
  because the parent's mode can override it.
  - Optional `if` filter on a hook (permission-rule syntax, one rule per hook):
  `"if": "Edit(**/specs/**)"`. Note that single-segment patterns like
  `Edit(specs/**)` are scoped to the working directory root, so `**/` is needed
  for any depth.

  **3. PreToolUse stdin JSON**
  Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md
  Common fields: `session_id`, `prompt_id`, `transcript_path`, `cwd`,
  `scratchpad_dir`, `permission_mode`, `effort` (object with `level`),
  `hook_event_name`.
  PreToolUse fields: `tool_name`, `tool_input` (for Bash: `command`,
  `description`, `timeout`, `run_in_background`), `tool_use_id`.
  Subagent identity: yes. For tool events fired by a subagent, the input carries
  `agent_id` ("Unique identifier for the subagent or in-process teammate the
  hook fires in") and `agent_type` (present when the session uses `--agent` or
  the hook fires inside a subagent).

  **4. settings.json PreToolUse schema and blocking**
  Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md
  ```json
  {
    "hooks": {
      "PreToolUse": [
        {
          "matcher": "Read|Edit|Write",
          "hooks": [
            { "type": "command",
              "command": "\"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\"/.claude/hooks/guard.sh" }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  }
  ```
  - Matcher rules: `"*"`, empty, or omitted matches all. Letters, digits, `_`,
  `-`, spaces, `,`, and `|` mean exact names or lists (`Edit|Write`, `Edit,
  Write`). Any other character makes it a JavaScript regex, unanchored (`^Edit$`
  for whole-string). Example from docs: `mcp__memory__.*`.
  - Optional `if` (single permission rule, PreToolUse only): `"if": "Bash(rm
  *)"`.
  - Block option 1: exit code 2 and write the reason to stderr. Exit 2 blocks
  the tool call, and stderr is the message shown.
  - Block option 2: exit 0 and print JSON to stdout:
  ```json
  {
    "hookSpecificOutput": {
      "hookEventName": "PreToolUse",
      "permissionDecision": "deny",
      "permissionDecisionReason": "Destructive command blocked by hook"
    }
  }
  ```
  Documented permissionDecision values are allow, deny, ask, and defer. The docs
  say to use one approach per hook. Exit 0 with no output means no decision,
  and silence does not approve the call.
  - Hook decisions do not bypass permission rules: a matching deny rule blocks
  even if the hook returns allow, and a matching ask rule still prompts.
  - `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`: supported. It is the project root where the session
  started, exported as an env var to the hook. The docs recommend quoting it in
  shell form, and exec form (`args`) for path placeholders. Example:
  `"${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/.claude/hooks/block-rm.sh"`.
  - The updatedInput output schema was not in the portion I could read.

  **5. Permission rules for .env files**
  Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions.md
  - Rule form: `Read(<gitignore-style path>)`. `Read(./.env)` matches the .env
  in the current directory. Bare `.env` or `**/.env` matches at any depth under
  the current directory, and does not match parent directories. `//**/.env`
  matches anywhere on the filesystem.
  - Evaluation order: deny, then ask, then allow. The first match wins, and
  specificity does not change order. An allow rule cannot carve an exception out
  of a deny. Hook `allow` does not override deny.
  - A `Read` deny also blocks Edit and Write on the same path.
  - Excluding `.env.example` from a broader deny: the docs support gitignore
  negation with `!`. "A deny or ask pattern that starts with `!` is a gitignore
  negation. It carves the paths it matches out of the `path` or `./path` rules
  listed before it." Their example: `Read(*.env)` followed by
  `Read(!sample.env)`. Analogous config (inferred from that example, not
  separately documented for `.env.*`):
  ```json
  { "permissions": { "deny": [ "Read(.env)", "Read(.env.*)",
  "Read(!.env.example)" ] } }
  ```
  The `!` rule must come after the rule it carves out, in the same settings
  file. A negation in project settings does not cancel a deny in managed
  settings.

  **6. Skills (.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md)**
  Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md
  Frontmatter must start on line 1 between `---` markers. All fields are
  optional, but `description` is recommended. Unknown fields are ignored in
  Claude Code.
  - `name`: defaults to directory name. Names with zero-width or control
  characters, `<`, or `>` are refused. No explicit length limit documented.
  - `description`: used for model triggering. If omitted, the first non-empty
  line is used. Combined `description` + `when_to_use` is truncated at 1,536
  chars in the listing.
  - `when_to_use`, `argument-hint`, `arguments`, `disable-model-invocation`
  (default false; also blocks subagent preload and session scheduled tasks),
  `user-invocable` (default true; false hides from / menu), `allowed-tools`
  (pre-approved for that turn; string or list; does not restrict tools),
  `disallowed-tools` (removed from pool while active), `model`, `effort`,
  `context: fork`, `agent` (used with fork; e.g. Explore, Plan,
  general-purpose), `background` (default true with fork), `hooks`, `paths`
  (glob activation), `shell` (bash or powershell), `metadata`, `license`,
  `compatibility` (up to 500 chars).
  - Portability: outside Claude Code (claude.ai uploads, Skills API), only
  `name`, `description`, `license`, `compatibility`, `metadata`, `allowed-tools`
  are accepted.
  - Supporting files: place them beside SKILL.md and link them from SKILL.md
  (e.g., `[reference.md](reference.md)`). Scripts are referenced with
  `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}`, often paired with `allowed-tools:
  Bash(${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/x.sh *)`. The docs recommend keeping SKILL.md
  under 500 lines.

  **7. Nested subagents**
  Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents.md
  Yes, by default. A subagent can spawn subagents up to three layers below the
  main conversation. Set `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH` to change the
  limit (1 disables nesting). To stop one subagent from spawning others, omit
  `Agent` from its `tools` or add it to `disallowedTools`.

  **8. Transcripts and /export**
  Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sessions.md
  - Path: `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session-id>.jsonl`. `<project>` is the
  working directory path with non-alphanumeric characters replaced by `-`. Paths
  over 200 chars are truncated and suffixed with a hash.
  - Format: JSONL, one object per line (messages, tool uses and results, request
  records, metadata). The format is internal and can change between versions,
  so the docs recommend `/export` or the script interfaces rather than parsing
  it directly.
  - Config: `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` moves storage. `CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME`
  names the project dir. `cleanupPeriodDays` (default 30 days) sets retention.
  `CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_PROMPT_HISTORY=1` suppresses writes.
  `--no-session-persistence` suppresses writes for one `claude -p` run. `claude
  purge` deletes project transcripts.
  - `/export`: opens a menu to copy the conversation to the clipboard or save it
  as a plain-text file, with messages and tool output rendered as readable
  text. Passing a filename (`/export out.txt`) skips the menu and writes to that
  file. The docs do not describe JSON or Markdown output.
  - Subagent transcript location: not documented in the pages I read.
  - For machine-readable output, the docs point to `claude -p --output-format
  json|stream-json` and `transcript_path` in hook input.

           that is not merged: a minimal form built from a Strapi-like JS
           ON with a **required number**, an **empty date**, a **select**
           , and a **legal-age validation**. It also checks how typing de
           grades with a runtime model. The findings feed an ADR (alterna
           tives, consequences); a human accepts it. | Production form co
           de for US-01 |
      119 +                                                              
      120 +The ADR backlog is in [adr/README.md](adr/README.md).         
      121 +                                                              
      122 +## 8. Agentic flow (summary — full detail in FLOW.md)         
      123 +                                                              
      124 +```                                                           
      125 +H0 intake (human) → 1 spec → HC1 → 2 ADRs → HC2 → 3 tests (red
          +) → 4 implementation                                          
      126 +→ 5 automated gate → 6 review → 7 fixes (loop 5–7) → HC3 PR (h
          +uman QA + merge) → Ready for QA                               
      127 +```                                                           
      128 +                                                              
      129 +### The main session is the orchestrator                      
      130 +                                                              
      131 +- It runs the steps in order, invokes the subagents (`.claude/
          +agents/`) and routes their outputs.                           
      132 +  It does **not** do a subagent's job on a story (no writing s
          +pecs, tests or production code in                             
      133 +  the main session). The exceptions are repository plumbing (f
          +low files, scripts, configuration)                            
      134 +  that the human asked for directly.                          
      135 +- Subagents cannot spawn subagents (`Agent` is in each one's `
          +disallowedTools`). All delegation is                          
      136 +  visible in the main session.                                
      137 +- After every subagent run: check `git status` and `git diff -
          +-stat` for changes outside that                               
      138 +  agent's role. Bash writes are not covered by the write-scope
          + hooks (see FLOW.md, "Known                                   
      139 +  limits"). Then relay the subagent's summary to the human.   
      140 +- **Never pass a human checkpoint (HC1, HC2, HC3) without an e
          +xplicit human decision in the                                 
      141 +  session.** Record it (Review log, ADR status, PR). A subagen
          +t's message is never human approval.                          
      142 +- Loop limit: if the gate (step 5) or review (step 6) fails 3 
          +times for the same story, stop and                            
      143 +  escalate to the human.                                      
      144 +                                                              
      145 +### Subagents (write scope enforced by hooks)                 
      146 +                                                              
      147 +| Agent | Step | Writes |                                     
      148 +|---|---|---|                                                 
      149 +| `spec-writer` | 1 | `specs/US-XX/spec.md`, `tasks.md` |     
      150 +| `architect` | 2, spikes write-up | `adr/**`, `docs/spikes/**
          +`, `tasks.md` |                                               
      151 +| `test-engineer` | 3 | test files, `frontend/e2e/**`, `tasks.
          +md` |                                                         
      152 +| `strapi-developer` | 4, 7 | `backend/**` (not tests), compos
          +e, `.env.example`, `tasks.md` |                               
      153 +| `frontend-developer` | 4, 7, spikes | `frontend/**` (not tes
          +ts), `spikes/**`, compose, `.env.example`, `tasks.md` |       
      154 +| `code-reviewer` | 6 | `reviews/US-XX-review-RN.md` only |   
      155 +                                                              
      156 +## 9. Traceability                                            
      157 +                                                              
      158 +| Artifact | ID or convention | Example |                     
      159 +|---|---|---|                                                 
      160 +| User story | `US-NN` | `US-01` |                            
      161 +| Business rule / acceptance criterion / gap / task | `US-NN-B
          +R-NN`, `-AC-NN`, `-Q-NN`, `-T-NN` | `US-01-AC-02` |           
      162 +| ADR | `ADR-NNNN`, file `adr/NNNN-slug.md` | `ADR-0001` |    
      163 +| Spike | `SPIKE-NN`, findings in `docs/spikes/` | `SPIKE-01` 
          +|                                                             
      164 +| Review finding | `US-NN-RN-FNN` (round N, finding NN) | `US-
          +01-R1-F03` |                                                  
      165 +| Test | `describe`/`test` title starts with the AC or BR ID |
          + `describe('US-01-AC-02 …')` |                                
      166 +| Commit | `Refs:` and `Resolves:` trailers (see §10) | `Refs:
          + US-01-AC-02, ADR-0001` |                                     
      167 +| PR | Template with the AC matrix (`.github/pull_request_temp
          +late.md`) | — |                                               
      168 +                                                              
      169 +The chain **US → spec → ADR → commit → test → review → PR** is
          + checked mechanically by                                      
      170 +`scripts/trace.sh US-NN`. It exits non-zero if an AC has no te
          +st (unless the spec marks it                                  
      171 +manual) or a blocker/major finding is open.                   
      172 +                                                              
      173 +## 10. Git conventions                                        
      174 +                                                              
      175 +- Branches: see §6 (`feat/us-01-slug`, `spike/01-forms`, `chor
          +e/…`, `docs/…`). Spike branches                               
      176 +  are never merged.                                           
      177 +- Commits: [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcomm
          +its.org/) in English,                                         
      178 +  `type(scope): summary`, with trailers:                      
      179 +  - `Refs: US-01-AC-02, ADR-0001` (required in `feat`, `fix` a
          +nd `test` commits of a story)                                 
      180 +  - `Resolves: US-01-R1-F03` (fix commits for review findings)
      181 +  - `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>` 
          +when an agent authored it                                     
      182 +- Small commits: one task (`US-NN-T-NN`) or one finding per co
          +mmit where practical. Tests and                               
      183 +  production code go in separate commits (they come from diffe
          +rent agents).                                                 
      184 +- Local identity only (`git config --local`). The author is th
          +e human; agents are co-authors.                               
      185 +- No pushes to `main`, no force pushes, and no `--no-verify` (
          +enforced by                                                   
      186 +  `.claude/hooks/guard-bash.mjs`). Changes reach `main` only t
          +hrough a PR merged by the human.                              
      187 +                                                              
      188 +## 11. Session continuity                                     
      189 +                                                              
      190 +Follow the `session-handoff` skill at the start and end of eve
          +ry session. The state of each story                           
      191 +lives in `specs/US-NN/tasks.md` (*Current step*, *Next action*
          +). Session logs are exported,                                 
      192 +unedited, to `logs/sessions/`.                                
      193 +                                                              
      194 +## 12. Definition of Done (Ready for QA)                      
      195 +                                                              
      196 +A story is **Ready for QA** when all of these hold:           
      197 +                                                              
      198 +- [ ] The spec is `Approved` (HC1), and the ADRs it needs are 
          +`Accepted` (HC2).                                             
      199 +- [ ] Every AC is implemented and has a passing automated test
          +, or a documented manual check.                               
      200 +- [ ] Lint, build, unit and e2e pass. `docker compose up` star
          +ts the stack with seed data for CO and CL.                    
      201 +- [ ] `scripts/trace.sh US-NN` exits 0, and `scripts/scan-secr
          +ets.sh` exits 0.                                              
      202 +- [ ] The last review round is `APPROVED`: no open blocker/maj
          +or findings; minors are fixed or justified.                   
      203 +- [ ] The human did a manual QA pass (both countries, keyboard
          + only, mobile width) and merged the PR (HC3).                 
      204 +- [ ] `tasks.md` shows `Ready for QA`, and the session logs ar
          +e exported.

✻ Brewed for 29s · done Friday 9:34 PM

› Message from spec-writer
  I've written the US-01 spec (v0.1) and its tasks file. Status is `Draft —
  awaiting HC1`, and 7 of the 26 gaps need a human answer before HC1. I did not
  run `scripts/trace.sh`. The test-mapping table keeps "manual" out of the level
  column, so the script will not count an AC as manual-only.

  ## 1. Files written (spec version 0.1)
  - `/Users/cristiansabogal/Proyectos/multicountry-car-insurance/specs/US-01/spe
  c.md`
  - `/Users/cristiansabogal/Proyectos/multicountry-car-insurance/specs/US-01/tas
  ks.md`: current step `1 Spec`, next action `HC1`, 29 tasks (T-01..T-29), each
  tied to ACs.

  ## 2. Counts
  - **Business rules:** 8 (BR-01..BR-08). BR-01..04 come from the story's rules.
  BR-05 and BR-06 come from the story context. BR-07 and BR-08 come from the
  Assessment ("same build serves CO and CL", "front-end persistence, no
  database").
  - **Acceptance criteria:** 27 in total: 4 from the story (AC-01..04, original
  titles kept) and 23 derived (AC-05..27). Every BR is covered by at least one
  AC, and every AC has a planned test level.
  - **Gaps:** 26 (Q-01..Q-26), 7 of them marked **[Blocks HC1]**.

  ## 3. Gaps that block HC1, with proposed defaults
  - **Q-01 [ADR] Country context:** the multi-country ADR decides. My proposal
  is a URL segment (`/co`, `/cl`). The root address shows a country chooser, and
  an unsupported code shows "Este país no está disponible." with links to both
  countries.
  - **Q-03 Seed field list:** use the seed in spec §7.2. CO gets 10 fields and
  CL gets 9, covering all five field types, with Spanish copy. CO uses "Línea"
  for the vehicle model and "Modelo (año)" for the year, because "modelo"
  usually means the year in Colombia.
  - **Q-04 Error messages:** each field has a required field-level
  `errorMessage`, plus optional per-rule overrides (including `required`). If no
  usable message reaches the front end, it shows "Revisa este campo." Messages
  are static text with no placeholders.
  - **Q-05 Vehicle year:** counted in calendar years with both limits inclusive,
  `Y−20 ≤ year ≤ Y+1` (2006–2027 today). The 20 and 1 are configurable
  `yearRange` rule parameters in Strapi.
  - **Q-08 Reserved keys:** these keys are reserved because US-02 and US-03
  depend on them: `documentType` (CO only), `documentNumber`, `fullName`,
  `birthDate`, `plate`, `make`, `model`, `vehicleYear`. Editors set each key
  once; it is unique per country and its format is enforced. If a reserved
  field, or the `minAge` rule, is missing, step 1 still works and logs a console
  warning.
  - **Q-09 RUT check digit:** yes. Add a code-backed rule kind `rutCheckDigit`
  (modulo 11, accepts dots and dash, `K`/`k`). If the answer is "no", AC-12 is
  retired.
  - **Q-15 [ADR] Persistence:** the persistence ADR decides. My proposal: the
  data survives step changes and a reload in the same tab (e.g.
  `sessionStorage`), is scoped to one country, and is cleared on tab close, on
  country switch and after payment. Nothing is stored across browser sessions.
  AC-21 is rewritten if the answer is "memory only".

  ## 4. ADRs needed
  1. **Multi-country content strategy:** the Strapi model for country-specific
  fields and how Angular resolves the country (root address, unsupported
  country, switching). Shared by US-01..03.
  2. **Forms library (SPIKE-01):** the spec stays library-agnostic. I propose
  the spike also covers loading stored values back into the form, dropping
  values of removed fields, when errors appear, focus on the first invalid
  field, and integer-only numbers.
  3. **Strapi access and security model:** public `find` vs a read-only proxy,
  runtime API URL, no caching that delays published changes, and how the e2e
  test for AC-03 writes content from the Node test process without a write token
  reaching the browser (Q-23).
  4. **Front-end persistence of wizard state:** Q-15, Q-02, and AC-04/20/21/22.
  - A fifth candidate, for the architect to fold into ADR 1 or write separately:
  **wizard routing and step guards** (step URLs, history entries, guard rule,
  focus on step change).

  ## Things the orchestrator should know
  - The spec refines the `dynamic-form-fields` skill contract v0 in five points
  (spec §7.4): a field-level `errorMessage` plus overrides, the `rutCheckDigit`
  rule kind, integer-only numbers, empty optional fields skipping all rules, and
  rules restricted by field type. The skill says it is updated in the same PR.
  I added task T-29 for the orchestrator, because no subagent can write to
  `.claude/`.
  - I used no ADR numbers in the spec, because none are assigned yet and
  `trace.sh` picks up any `ADR-NNNN` it finds. The skill

  ## Decisions and the strongest argument against each

  **ADR-0001: multi-country content strategy and country context.** Chosen:
  option A (a `country` collection type, plus a required `manyToOne` `country`
  relation on `form-field`, `plan` and `terms`) and R1 (the country in the URL
  path).
  - **Strapi side:**
    - A `country` entry holds `code`, `name`, `currencyCode`, `locale` and
  `sortOrder`.
    - `config/api.ts` sets `documents.strictRelations: true`, so Strapi refuses
  to publish an item with no country.
    - `key` uniqueness per country is enforced by a Document Service middleware,
  because Strapi's `unique` is global.
  - **Angular side:**
    - The list of supported countries comes from Strapi (published `country`
  entries), loaded once per page load. There are no country literals in code.
    - `/` shows a chooser. `/ar/...` shows "Este país no está disponible." with
  links to each country. If the country list cannot be loaded, an error with
  "Reintentar" is shown instead, so the app never wrongly says a country is
  unavailable.
    - Entering another country's context discards the stored data (Q-02).
  - **Routing (T-06 folded in):**
    - Routes are `/:country/datos`, `/:country/planes` and `/:country/resumen`.
    - `planes` has `children: []` and no component, guarded by `wizardStepGuard`
  (a `CanActivateFn`).
    - When step 1 data is missing or invalid, the guard sends the user back to
  `/<country>/datos` with `RedirectCommand` and `replaceUrl`, so the blocked
  address does not stay in history.
    - Step slugs are Spanish because users see them.
  - **Strongest argument against:** option B (i18n locales `es-CO`/`es-CL`)
  gives per-country uniqueness for free (Strapi's unique check is scoped by
  locale, verified) and lets editors copy one country's content to another.
  Option A needs custom code for uniqueness and has no copy tool. The country
  list being content also means the chooser and the unknown-country page now
  depend on Strapi being reachable.

  **ADR-0002: Strapi access and security.** Chosen: option 2, a same-origin
  nginx proxy plus the Strapi public role.
  - **Proxy and front-end build:**
    - nginx serves the Angular build and proxies only GET requests on
  allow-listed `/api/` paths.
    - It sends `Cache-Control: no-store` on API responses and rejects any
  `Authorization` header.
    - The build uses the relative path `/api`, so no runtime config file is
  needed. The upstream address is set through the nginx image's env templates.
  - **Public role:** exactly `find` on `country` and `form-field`, with no
  `findOne`. The users-permissions defaults on the public role (`auth.register`
  and others) are removed and `allow_register` is set to false.
  - **Strapi hardening:**
    - A global middleware forces published content on anonymous reads.
    - CORS is closed to an env-driven allow-list.
    - The default "Full Access" token is deleted.
  - **AC-03 test writes:** the Playwright Node process logs in to the admin API
  with fictitious dev admin credentials, which bootstrap creates from env vars.
  It creates a `custom` token scoped to form-field create/delete, POSTs directly
  to Strapi's port (a REST POST publishes by default), then deletes the field
  and the token.
  - **Strongest argument against:** Strapi's own port (open for the admin panel)
  still answers the public `find` endpoints and skips the proxy's allow-list.
  Keeping drafts hidden there relies on custom middleware that a Strapi upgrade
  could quietly make incomplete. Option 3 (proxy-injected token, empty public
  role) would close that port to anonymous reads.

  **ADR-0003: wizard state persistence.** Chosen: `sessionStorage`.
  - **What is stored:** one versioned key, `quote-wizard`, owned only by
  `QuoteStore`. It holds one country, the step 1 values in the §7.3 shape and
  later the plan id.
    - The field configuration is not stored; it is fetched again on each page
  load. This closes the open point in spec §7.3.
    - Values are written on every change.
    - On reading, the entry is checked first; values for removed fields or
  options are dropped (AC-23).
  - **Clearing:** on tab close (the browser does it), on switching country, and
  on successful payment (US-03's job). It is not cleared on a rejected payment.
  - **Privacy:** values are never logged, sent or put in the URL. There is no
  client-side encryption, because the key would sit next to the data. If storage
  is unavailable, the store falls back to memory.
  - **Strongest argument against:** the document number and birth date stay in
  clear text in tab storage while the tab is open, readable by any script on the
  origin. MDN says the session survives browser "restores", so a restored
  session can bring them back. Option 1 (memory only) avoids this completely, at
  the cost of losing data on reload.

  ## Facts verified
  - **Strapi 5.63.0 packages** (`npm pack` into the scratchpad, never into the
  repo):
    - REST defaults to `status=published` only when the parameter is absent, and
  `status=draft` is accepted from any caller with `find`. The docs page states
  no permission requirement. This is why ADR-0002 adds the published-only
  middleware.
    - Non-localised i18n fields are copied to every locale.
    - The unique check is scoped by locale.
    - `strictRelations` defaults to false.
    - Filtering through a relation needs `find` on the target type.
    - users-permissions defaults (`DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS`, `allow_register:
  true`).
    - API token types and lifespans, and token keys generated randomly.
    - The default token is created on a fresh database.
    - CORS default is `origin: '*'`.
  - **Angular 22.3.0:** the `CanActivateFn`, `GuardResult`, `RedirectCommand`
  and `provideAppInitializer` typings, and the route validation rules
  (`children: []` is valid; `redirectTo` cannot be combined with guards).
  - **Other docs:** MDN on `sessionStorage`, and the Docker Hub docs for the
  nginx image's env templates.

  ## Could not verify
  - That a Strapi global middleware that rewrites the query really overrides
  `status` before the content API validates and sanitises the query. I checked
  the rule, not a running implementation. The Confirmation test in ADR-0002
  covers it.
  - That `publicationFilter` or `hasPublishedVersion` can expose drafts on their
  own. I strip them as a precaution.
  - The nginx directives themselves (method limits, rejecting `Authorization`),
  beyond the documented template mechanism. They are not checked against a
  running container.
  - I did not cross-check Strapi admin API behaviour (`/admin/login` response
  shape, `/admin/api-tokens`) beyond the 5.63.0 route and controller source.
  These are internal admin endpoints with no stability promise.
  - I did not confirm the absence of `Cache-Control` from Strapi content API
  responses at runtime. A grep of `@strapi/core` dist only (no hits) does not
  cover other plugins or middlewares.

  ## Points where the ADRs force a change to the approved spec (spec not edited)
  1. Spec §7.3 types `country` as `'CO' | 'CL'`. Under ADR-0001 the country list
  is content, so this becomes an ISO alpha-2 code checked against the loaded
  countries.
  2. Spec §8 has no state for "the country list could not be loaded" on the
  chooser and the unknown-country page, and the copy for it is undecided. "No
  pudimos cargar el formulario…" is specific to the form. The links in AC-17 do
  not appear in that state.
  3. ADR-0002 adds a security check: an anonymous `?status=draft` request must
  not return the seeded draft field, and a POST through nginx must get 405. No
  AC covers it; AC-13 is UI only. I placed it in the existing
  `us-01-security.spec.ts`, which keeps the four-file e2e limit, but tracing it
  needs a new AC or a decision to leave it as a non-traced check.
  4. ADR-0002 adds bootstrap behaviour that no spec task describes yet:
     - Create a dev super admin from
  `STRAPI_ADMIN_EMAIL`/`STRAPI_ADMIN_PASSWORD`.
     - Delete the default Full Access token.
     - Set `allow_register` to false.
     - Add the published-only middleware.
     - Set the CORS allow-list.

     T-18 and T-19 probably need re-scoping after HC2. T-20's "runtime API URL
  configuration" becomes "relative `/api` plus nginx/dev-server proxy".
  5. No conflict with AC-21: ADR-0003 keeps it as written, so the "memory only"
  rewrite the spec planned for does not apply.
  6. Spec §11 says the AC-17 unit file is "per the multi-country ADR". ADR-0001
  names it `supported-country-guard.spec.ts`.

  (an interactive prompt).

  API facts were read from the installed
  `node_modules/@angular/forms/types/_structure-chunk.d.ts` and `signals.d.ts`,

  ## Shared, library-agnostic module (`src/app/core/`)

  - Pure functions, with no Angular import except the `CLOCK` token
  (`InjectionToken<() => Date>`).
  - The functions are `parseFieldConfigs`, `validateField(cfg, value, today)`,
  `hydrate`, `toOutput`, `parseIsoDate` and `ageOn`.
  - `validateField` applies required, the optional-empty skip, integer-only,
  then the rules in config order. The first failing message wins.
  - Both adapters call the same `validateField` from one custom validator per
  field.
  - The spike did not exercise the built-in validators (`required()`, `min()`,
  `pattern()` / `Validators.*`).
  - Core semantics are tested once in `core.spec.ts` (8 tests) and again through
  the DOM in each library.

  ## Criteria table

  Test names are `[lib] (x)` in `src/app/specs/criteria.spec.ts`. The same title
  runs for both libraries.

  | # | Criterion | Signal Forms (`@angular/forms/signals`) | Reactive Forms
  (`FormRecord`) |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | a | Required number: empty vs `0` vs value; integer only | Works. The model
  value is a **string** (`''` is empty). `validate()` calls the shared function.
  `<input type="number">` with a string model falls through to `element.value`.
  Gotcha: with a `number` model, a cleared native input writes `null`, and
  decimals (`2020.5`) reach the model. Integer-only is therefore a validator,
  not a type (`library-facts.spec.ts`). Test: `[signal-forms] (a)`. | Works
  after a workaround. `NumberValueAccessor` (selected by
  `input[type=number][formControl]`) writes `number\|null` into the control even
  when it is declared `FormControl<string\|boolean>`. The empty check treated
  numeric `2020` as empty until a `normalise()` step was added in the adapter
  (validator input and output mapping). `nonNullable: true` does not stop the
  accessor from writing `null`. Not tried: forcing `DefaultValueAccessor`.
  Tests: `[reactive-forms] (a)`, `(e)`, and `library-facts.spec.ts`. |
  | b | Empty date: required vs optional; empty optional valid and skips
  `minAge` | Works. Date held as `''` / ISO string. `<input type="date">` with a
  string model falls through to `element.value`. Optional empty is valid and
  the rule is skipped. Once filled, the rule runs. Test: `[signal-forms] (b)`. |
  Works, same behaviour. `DefaultValueAccessor` handles `type=date` as a
  string. Test: `[reactive-forms] (b)`. |
  | c | Select: required, nothing pre-selected | Works. Model `''` plus a
  placeholder `<option value="">`. `select.value === ''` and `selectedIndex ===
  0`. Options render in `sortOrder`. Test: `[signal-forms] (c)`. | Works, same.
  Test: `[reactive-forms] (c)`. |
  | d | Legal age with injectable clock | Works. `CLOCK` is provided in TestBed
  and the validator closes over it. 18th birthday today is valid, tomorrow is
  invalid (2026-11-20). 29 Feb is covered in `core.spec.ts`. Test:
  `[signal-forms] (d)`. | Works, same. Test: `[reactive-forms] (d)`. |
  | e | Typing with a runtime-built model | Static model: precise keys and
  types, and an unknown key is a compile error. Runtime `Record<string,
  string\|boolean>`: any key compiles (not `undefined`), and at runtime
  `f['unknown']()` throws `TypeError`. The value is the union, and the union
  does not compile against native controls (see Typing). Needed a cast helper.
  Tests: `typing.spec.ts`, `[signal-forms] (e)`. | Static `FormGroup`: precise.
  Runtime `FormRecord<FormControl<string\|boolean>>`: `controls[key]` is
  `FormControl<string\|boolean>` (runtime `undefined` for an unknown key),
  `get(key)` is `AbstractControl\|null`, `getRawValue()` is `Record<string,
  string\|boolean>`. `[formControl]` accepts the union with no cast. The runtime
  number control value is `number\|null`. Tests: `typing.spec.ts`,
  `[reactive-forms] (e)`. |
  | f | Hydration from stored values | Works. The model signal is created from
  `hydrate(configs, stored)` before `form()`. Stored number `2020` becomes
  `'2020'`. Pristine, untouched, no errors shown on entry. The DOM shows the
  values (input, select, checkbox). A stored select value no longer in the
  options keeps its value, the select shows the placeholder, and the form is
  invalid. Tests: `[signal-forms] (f)` x2. | Works. Controls are created from
  `hydrate(...)`, with the same results. Tests: `[reactive-forms] (f)` x2. |
  | g | Drop stored values of keys no longer configured | Works only because
  `hydrate()` filters by config before the model exists. The model signal is the
  source of truth: an extra key written into it stays in `form().value()`
  (`library-facts.spec.ts`). A config change rebuilds the whole form from
  `stored`, so values typed since mount are lost unless the caller keeps
  `stored` current. Test: `[signal-forms] (g)`. | Works through the same
  `hydrate()`. `FormGroup.setValue` with an extra key **throws**, and
  `patchValue` ignores it. Config change rebuilds, with the same loss of typed
  values. Test: `[reactive-forms] (g)`. |
  | h | When errors become visible | `submit()` calls `markAsTouched()` on the
  root, which propagates to all fields. One condition (`touched() && invalid()`)
  covers blur and failed submit. Typing alone does not touch. After a failed
  submit there are 3 alerts (birthDate, make, vehicleYear) and the optional
  fields stay quiet. `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby` are bound. Test:
  `[signal-forms] (h)`. | Needs an explicit `record.markAllAsTouched()` in the
  submit handler (removing it fails the test). `touched` is a plain property,
  not a signal. Re-render worked because blur and `ngSubmit` are template
  listeners (zoneless). Same visible behaviour. Test: `[reactive-forms] (h)`. |
  | i | Focus first invalid field after failed submit | Works with a built-in
  API. `onInvalid` runs `root[key]().focusBoundControl()` on the first invalid
  field in `sortOrder`. `document.activeElement` was verified over 3 consecutive
  attempts. Test: `[signal-forms] (i)`. | No focus API on controls. Workaround:
  `host.querySelector('#'+key).focus()` (id equals the key). Same result. Test:
  `[reactive-forms] (i)`. |
  | j | Output maps empty optional to `null`, model stays non-null | Works. The
  model is `Record<string, string\|boolean>` (`''` / `false`) and `toOutput()`
  produces `null`, an integer, or trimmed text. The model keeps what was typed
  (`'   '` stays in the model, the output is `null`). Test: `[signal-forms]
  (j)`. | Works with the same `toOutput()`, after the `normalise()` workaround
  from (a). Test: `[reactive-forms] (j)`. |

  Checkbox note: an unchecked optional checkbox is output as `false`, not
  `null`. The skill table says "empty optional field -> null" but also lists
  boolean for checkbox (open question 5).

  ## Typing observations

  - **Signal Forms, static model** `signal({vehicleYear:'',
  acceptsOffers:false})`:
    - `f.vehicleYear().value()` is `string`.
    - `f.nope` and `.value.set(2020)` are compile errors.
  - **Signal Forms, runtime model** `signal<Record<string, string|boolean>>`:
    - `f['anything']` compiles as `FieldTree<string|boolean>`.
    - At runtime an unknown key throws `TypeError: f.<key> is not a function`.
  - **Signal Forms, template binding of the union fails to compile.** Captured
  `ng build` errors:
    - text: `TS2322: Type 'WritableSignal<RawValue>' is not assignable to type
  '{ (): string; set: (v: string) => void; } | { (): number | null; set: (v:
  number | null) => void; }'`
    - checkbox: `Type 'RawValue' is not assignable to type 'boolean'`
    - number: `Type 'RawValue' is not assignable to type 'string | number |
  null'`
    - date: `Type 'RawValue' is not assignable to type 'string | number | Date |
  null'`
    - `FieldTree<string|boolean>` is not assignable to `FieldTree<string>` (a
  `@ts-expect-error` holds).
    - Workaround used: `str(key)` / `bool(key)` accessors doing `as unknown as
  FieldTree<string>` / `FieldTree<boolean>` (2 casts).
  - **Native control accepted types in Signal Forms:** text takes `string`,
  number takes `string|number|null`, date takes `string|number|Date|null`,
  checkbox takes `boolean`.
  - **Reactive Forms, `FormRecord<FormControl<string|boolean>>`:**
    - `controls[key]` is `FormControl<string|boolean>`, with no `undefined`
  because `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` is off.
    - `get(key)` is nullable.
    - `setValue(5)` is a compile error.
    - The template `[formControl]` binding compiles with no casts.
  - **Both libraries:** the types describe the model, not what native controls
  write at runtime (`null` from cleared number inputs).
  - **`form()` inside `computed()`:** it throws `NG0602: effect() cannot be
  called from within a reactive context`, because `form()` creates an effect.
  The adapter wraps it in `untracked(() => form(...))`. Building a `FormRecord`
  inside `computed()` had no such issue.
  - **`form()` injection:** it needs an injection context or `{ injector }` in
  its options.

  ## Open questions / unverified

  1. All runs were in jsdom. Not verified in a real browser: focus and scroll
  behaviour, native `date` and `number` UI, `badInput` handling
  (`NativeInputParseError` is in the source but was not exercised), mobile
  keyboards, and screen reader announcements of `role="alert"`.
  2. Blur was simulated with `new FocusEvent('blur')` and typing with `input`
  plus `change` events. Real event ordering is not covered.
  3. Forcing a string model in Reactive Forms with `DefaultValueAccessor` (for
  example `type="text" inputmode="numeric"`, or a custom accessor) was not
  tried.
  4. `rutCheckDigit` is not implemented.
  5. Output for an unchecked optional checkbox is `false` in the spike. The spec
  must say `false` or `null`.
  6. A config change while mounted rebuilds the form from `stored` in both
  libraries, so values typed since mount are lost. Whether step 1 can change
  config while mounted (a country switch) is a spec question.
  7. Async validators and `submit({ ignoreValidators })` were not exercised.
  8. A dynamic `[type]` binding together with `[formField]` was avoided (static
  `@switch` branches), so it is unverified.
  9. Bundle size, performance with many fields, and SSR were not measured.
  10. Error visibility is hand-built in both (`touched && invalid`).
  `provideSignalFormsConfig` (class and ARIA auto-binding) was not explored.
  11. The vendored `signal-forms.md` forbids `null` in the model. The spike
  confirms that a non-null model with `null` only in the mapped output works. It
  also shows `null` can still appear at runtime in a `number` model through
  native inputs (row a).

  library.md`, status `Proposed`.
    - **Decision:** step 1 uses Signal Forms (`@angular/forms/signals` 22.3.0)
  on top of a shared validation layer that does not depend on any forms library.
    - **Options considered:** (1) Signal Forms, (2) Reactive Forms with
  `FormRecord`, (3) no forms library, with native inputs bound to plain signals.
    - **Main rules it sets:**
      - Each field gets one `validate()` that calls the pure validation
  function. The library's built-in validators are not used.
      - The form holds a `Record<string, string | boolean>`. Number fields hold
  strings (`''` means empty), so the model is never `null`. This departs from
  the vendored skill's "use 0 for numbers".
      - A pure `toOutput()` produces the §7.3 values.
      - Stored values are filtered by the current config before `form()` is
  called.
      - The form is built once per config load, never inside `computed()`.
      - An error shows when the field is `touched() && invalid()`. `submit()`
  marks every field as touched, and `onInvalid` + `focusBoundControl()` moves
  focus to the first invalid field in sortOrder.
      - Only two narrowing casts are allowed in templates.
      - Confirmation is a grep that bans Reactive Forms imports, plus named
  component tests.

  ## 2. Strongest argument against the chosen option
  Signal Forms has been public API only since 22.0.0 (2026-06-03), about five
  and a half months. The CHANGELOG lists 39 fix, perf or feat entries in the
  `forms` scope from 22.0.0 to 22.3.0. All the spike evidence comes from jsdom.

  Its typing benefit also mostly disappears for a form built at runtime: the
  template needed casts. Reactive Forms (`FormRecord`) is the long-established
  path for runtime-keyed forms, compiled with no casts, and rejects stale keys
  in `setValue` by throwing.

  The ADR answers this as follows:
  - Only a small set of APIs is used, all tagged `@publicApi 22.0`.
  - The validation rules live outside the library, so switching later means
  rewriting one component of about 110 lines.
  - The Reactive Forms adapter needed `normalise()` to fix a real bug (a valid
  year was read as empty).

  ## 3. Not verified
  - **jsdom only:** real-browser focus, the native date and number UI,
  `badInput`, and screen reader announcement of `role="alert"` are unchecked.
  The `1e` → `''` behaviour is from the HTML spec's value sanitisation, not
  tested.
  - **Option 3 was not built.** It is assessed only from the fact that the
  shared validation code worked without any forms API.
  - **angular.dev quotes:** the Signal Forms overview page is unversioned, and
  the quotes came through a WebFetch summary.
  - **Changelog count:** the 39 entries are the whole `forms` scope, not only
  Signal Forms changes.
  - **Not exercised in the spike:** `provideSignalFormsConfig`, a dynamic
  `[type]` binding with `[formField]`, async validators, `rutCheckDigit`, bundle
  size.

  **Verified:**
  - npm: `latest` is 22.3.0, published 2026-11-18; 22.0.0 was published
  2026-06-03.
  - CHANGELOG: 22.0.0 includes commit `7745365910`, "graduate signal forms APIs
  to public API".
  - The published 22.3.0 typings, read through `npm pack` into the scratchpad:
    - `form`, `submit`, `FormField`, `FormRoot`, `validate`, `FieldState` (which
  declares `focusBoundControl`), `FormSubmitOptions` and
  `provideSignalFormsConfig` are tagged `@publicApi 22.0`.
    - The only `@experimental` items are the WebMCP ones.
    - `FormRecord` and `ReactiveFormsModule` are `@publicApi` and not
  deprecated.
  - The compiled `submit` calls `node.markAsTouched()`.

  ## Spec impacts (I did not edit the spec)
  - **Unchecked optional checkbox (open question 5):** §7.3 says both "checkbox
  → boolean" and "empty optional → `null`". The spike outputs `false`. The spec
  should choose one; I recommend `false`, because a checkbox has no empty state.
  - **Config change while mounted (open question 6):** the spec already mostly
  settles this (Q-16: config is fetched once per full page load). ADR-0001 has
  no in-app link between `/co/datos` and `/cl/datos`, but Angular would reuse
  the component if that navigation happened, so ADR-0004 requires a new
  component instance per country. ADR-0003 saves values on every change, so
  rebuilding from the store loses nothing. No spec change is needed unless the
  human wants this written down.
  - **Conflict with ADR-0003:** ADR-0003 writes values to the store "on every
  change, valid or not" in the §7.3 shape, where a number is an integer. An
  in-progress invalid value such as `2015.5` or `abc` cannot be stored as an
  integer. Either the store keeps the raw editing value until the step is valid,
  or §7.3 applies only to the value handed over on a valid "Continuar". This
  needs a decision at HC2, as a spec clarification or a note on ADR-0003. I did
  not edit ADR-0003.
  - **Wrong message for unparseable numbers:** unparseable number input reads as
  empty, so it shows the "required" message instead of the format message. Is
  that acceptable under AC-09? It is worth a quick check at HC2 or in the e2e
  test.

  Ya puedes hacer HC2: aceptación de los ADRs 0001–0004.

  Los 4 ADRs

  ADR: 0001 Multi-país
  Decisión propuesta: En Strapi, una colección country (código, moneda,
    locale) y una relación obligatoria hacia campos, planes y términos. En
    Angular, el país va en la URL (/:country/datos, /planes, /resumen); la
    lista de países viene de Strapi; / muestra un selector y un país
    desconocido muestra el mensaje de "no disponible". El paso 2 es una ruta
    vacía con su guard, y cambiar de país borra los datos.
  Argumento más fuerte en contra (según el architect): Con i18n (un locale por
    país), la unicidad de la clave por país vendría gratis y los editores
    podrían copiar contenido de un país a otro. La opción elegida necesita
    código propio para la unicidad, y el selector depende de que Strapi
    responda.
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  ADR: 0002 Seguridad
  Decisión propuesta: Un proxy nginx en el mismo origen que solo deja pasar
    GET a rutas permitidas de /api/, con no-store y rechazando Authorization.
    El rol público solo tiene find sobre country y form-field. Además: un
    middleware que fuerza contenido publicado, CORS cerrado, se borra el token
    "Full Access" y se desactiva el registro. El e2e de AC-03 crea un token
    temporal con credenciales de admin de desarrollo ficticias.
  Argumento más fuerte en contra (según el architect): El puerto propio de
    Strapi, abierto para el panel de admin, también responde los find públicos
    y se salta el proxy. Ocultar los borradores ahí depende de un middleware
    propio que una actualización de Strapi podría romper sin avisar. La opción
    3 (el proxy inyecta el token y el rol público queda vacío) cerraría ese
    hueco.
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  ADR: 0003 Persistencia
  Decisión propuesta: sessionStorage en una sola clave versionada, de la que
    solo es dueño el QuoteStore. No guarda la configuración, solo los valores,
    y al leer descarta los campos que ya no existen. Se borra al cerrar la
    pestaña, al cambiar de país y tras pagar. Sin cifrado, porque la clave
    viviría junto a los datos.
  Argumento más fuerte en contra (según el architect): El documento y la fecha
    de nacimiento quedan en claro mientras la pestaña está abierta, y un
    navegador que restaura la sesión los recupera. La opción de guardar solo
    en memoria lo evita, a cambio de perder los datos al recargar.
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  ADR: 0004 Formularios
  Decisión propuesta: Signal Forms sobre una capa de validación propia que no
    depende de la librería. El modelo no admite null: los números se guardan
    como texto y se convierten al salir. Para el foco en el primer error usa
    focusBoundControl(), y solo se permiten 2 casts en plantillas.
  Argumento más fuerte en contra (según el architect): Solo lleva 5,5 meses
    como API estable (con 39 cambios en forms desde 22.0), toda la evidencia
    del spike viene de jsdom, y con un modelo construido en tiempo de
    ejecución pierde la ventaja de tipado. Mitigación: cambiar de librería
    costaría reescribir un componente de unas 110 líneas.

  Puntos donde los ADRs obligan a ajustar la spec aprobada (10)

  1. §7.3: el país deja de ser 'CO' | 'CL' y pasa a ser un código ISO validado
     contra la lista que llega de Strapi.
  2. §8: falta el estado "no se pudo cargar la lista de países", con su texto.
  3. ADR-0002 añade una comprobación de seguridad que ningún AC cubre: una
     petición anónima con ?status=draft no debe devolver borradores, y un POST
     tiene que recibir 405. ¿Se crea un AC nuevo, o queda como comprobación sin
     trazar?
  4. ADR-0002 añade al bootstrap: el admin de desarrollo, el borrado del token
     por defecto, el registro desactivado, el middleware y CORS. Hay que
     re-asignar T-18, T-19 y T-20.
  5. AC-21 se mantiene tal cual. Solo es información, no requiere cambio.
  6. AC-17 pasa a tener un archivo de test unitario con nombre propio.
  7. Un checkbox opcional sin marcar, ¿se guarda como false o como null? El
     architect recomienda false.
  8. Un cambio de configuración con el formulario montado no requiere cambiar la
     spec.
  9. Conflicto entre ADR-0003 y §7.3: el store guarda en cada cambio, pero un
     valor a medio escribir como 2015.5 no cabe como entero. Las alternativas:
     guardar el valor crudo mientras se edita, o aplicar la forma de §7.3 solo
     al pulsar "Continuar".
  10. Un número que no se puede interpretar se lee como vacío y muestra el
      mensaje de "obligatorio" en lugar del de formato. ¿Es aceptable para
      AC-09?

  Mis hallazgos como orquestador

  - H1: como dije arriba, el argumento más fuerte en contra no aparece en los
    ADRs, aunque FLOW.md lo pide para HC2. Propongo añadir una sección Strongest
    argument against a la plantilla adr-madr y a los cuatro ADRs.
  - H2: en el primer lote, el architect editó tasks.md vía Bash. Él mismo lo
    declaró y lo confirmé con el diff. En el segundo lote usó Edit, como le
    pedí. Lo registraré en FLOW.md como el límite conocido observado en la
    práctica.
  - H3: el ADR-0004 contradice a la skill de Angular ("usa 0 para números").
    Está bien según la regla de precedencia, pero conviene que lo sepas.

  Cómo responder

  Para cada ADR: Accepted, Rejected o cambios. Para los puntos 1–4, 7, 9 y 10,
  tu decisión. Para H1, si lo apruebas. Si alguno de los puntos cambia la spec,
  el spec-writer hace la v0.3 (solo toca spec.md) y la vuelves a ver en HC1.
  Nada se commitea hasta tu decisión.

  What each subsection says:

  - **ADR-0001:** Option B (i18n locales) makes field keys unique per country
  without custom code, because Strapi checks uniqueness per locale (verified in
  `@strapi/core@5.63.0`), and it lets editors copy one country's content to
  another. With option A we have to write and maintain that uniqueness code,
  there is no copy tool, and the country chooser and the unknown-country page
  depend on Strapi being reachable.
    - Why we accept it: B copies non-localised fields to every locale on save
  (verified in `@strapi/i18n@5.63.0`), so one wrong setting on a price
  overwrites the other country's price. B also mixes language with market. The
  mitigations are the uniqueness middleware with a test, dropping duplicates in
  the front end (AC-14), and a "Reintentar" error instead of a wrong "not
  available".
  - **ADR-0002:** Strapi's own port still answers the public `find` endpoints
  and skips the proxy's allow-list. Keeping drafts hidden there relies on custom
  middleware that a Strapi upgrade could quietly make incomplete. Option 3
  would close that port to anonymous reads.
    - Why we accept it: the data on those endpoints is public, and the public
  role has no other permission. Option 3 breaks the single start command (D4),
  and through the proxy it gives the browser the same access. An automated
  anonymous request for a draft field checks the draft rule, re-run on every
  Strapi upgrade.
  - **ADR-0003:** The document number and birth date stay in clear text in tab
  storage while the tab is open, readable by any script on the origin. MDN says
  the session survives browser "restores", so a restored session can bring them
  back. Option 1 (memory only) avoids this completely.
    - Why we accept it: memory only fails the reload behaviour in AC-21 (D2)
  and, through the AC-19 guard, sends the person back to an empty step 1. There
  are no third-party scripts, values are never logged, the data is cleared on
  payment and on country switch, and the remaining risk is accepted for a quote
  flow without accounts.
  - **ADR-0004:** Signal Forms has been public API for only about 5.5 months
  (22.0.0), with 39 forms-scope changes through 22.3.0. All the spike evidence
  comes from jsdom. The typing benefit mostly disappears for a runtime form: the
  template needed casts, and an unknown key compiles but throws at runtime.
  Reactive Forms `FormRecord` is the long-established path, needs no casts, and
  `setValue` throws on stale keys.
    - Why we accept it: only APIs tagged `@publicApi 22.0` are used, on a pinned
  22.3.0. Validation lives outside the library, so switching means rewriting
  one component of about 110 lines (D8). The Reactive version needed
  `normalise()` to fix a real bug (D5). The CO e2e test (US-01-T-11) and the HC3
  screen reader check cover the gap left by jsdom.

  The "Why we accept it" paragraphs only reuse mitigations and reasons already
  in each ADR's Consequences and Pros/Cons sections, and the driver references
  (D2, D3, D4, D5, D8) match each ADR's own *Decision Drivers* list. No new
  facts were added, so there was nothing new to verify.

  1. **Country type (ADR-0001):** §7.3 `country` is an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code
  checked against the published `country` entries loaded from Strapi. The
  glossary, §2 and BR-07 match it. The seed and the examples are unchanged.
  2. **Country list could not be loaded (ADR-0001):**
     - §8 has two new states for the root chooser and the unknown-country page:
  "Country list loading" and "Country list unavailable". The second shows the
  error with "Reintentar" and never "Este país no está disponible.".
     - The "Unsupported country" state now applies only once the list has
  loaded.
     - AC-17 now starts from a loaded list, and has a second scenario for a
  failed list load at `/`, `/ar/datos` and `/co/datos`.

  fits better than BR-07.
     - Anonymous `status=draft` requests return no seeded `email` field, both on
  Strapi's own port and through the proxy.
     - `POST /api/form-fields` through the proxy returns 405, and nothing is
  created (checked by reading key `securityProbe` back anonymously).
     - The e2e test goes in `us-01-security.spec.ts` and runs from the Node
  process. §11 and BR-06's coverage column are updated.

  5. **§11:** AC-17's unit file is now `supported-country-guard.spec.ts`.
  6. **Checkbox:** an unchecked optional checkbox gives `false`, never `null`.
  "Empty optional field → `null`" now applies only to text, number, select and
  date.
  7. **Store shape (ADR-0003):**
     - §7.3 now has two shapes: the stored raw editing values, and the typed
  output produced only on a valid "Continuar". BR-08 and the glossary match.
     - AC-18 now says "typed step 1 output" and has a new scenario: an invalid
  "Continuar" produces no typed output.
     - AC-21 now says `sessionStorage` applies, and has a new scenario: an
  unfinished step 1 (`'2015.5'`) comes back exactly as typed after a reload.
     - AC-23's preamble is updated. AC-20 had no conflict and is unchanged.
  8. **AC-09 (ADR-0004):** a new scenario and note. A number the browser cannot
  parse (`abc`, `1e`) reaches the model as empty: a required field shows
  `requiredMessage`, else `errorMessage`; an optional field is treated as empty.
  The CO e2e test confirms it in a real browser by typing `1e` key by key in
  "Modelo (año)". Because CO "Modelo (año)" has no `requiredMessage`, it shows
  the field-level message.

✻ Brewed for 23s · done Friday 11:13 PM

❯ estas haciedno test si todavia no hay app?                                    

⏺ Sí, es intencional. Es el paso 3 del flujo que aprobaste en FLOW.md, tests 
  primero: el test-engineer escribe los tests antes de que exista la app, y
  todos empiezan en rojo, fallando.

  Por qué en este orden

  - Los tests salen de la spec, no del código. Si se escribieran después, el
    agente tendería a comprobar lo que el código hace y no lo que la spec pide.
    Escribiéndolos antes, un test en rojo significa "este criterio de aceptación
    todavía no se cumple".
  - Las responsabilidades quedan separadas. El hook impide que los
    desarrolladores editen tests. En el paso 4 su trabajo es poner los tests en
    verde, no reescribirlos para que pasen.
  - Los imports de los tests definen la API. Le pedí la lista de módulos y
    funciones que esperan sus tests (field-validators, QuoteStore,
    wizardStepGuard…), y eso es lo que implementan después el frontend-developer
    y el strapi-developer.
  - La trazabilidad existe desde el principio. Cada test lleva el ID de su
    criterio de aceptación, así que trace.sh puede comprobar ya que los 28
    tienen un test asignado.

  Qué significa "rojo" ahora mismo

  - Unitarios y de componente: fallan porque los módulos importados no existen.
    Le exigí demostrar con tsc que ese es el único error (TS2307). Cualquier
    otro error sería un fallo del propio test.
  - e2e: no se pueden ejecutar todavía, porque aún no se sirve la app (falta
    nginx, T-35). Solo se comprueba que Playwright los carga (--list). Se
    ejecutan de verdad al final del paso 4, en el gate automático.

  Para esto pedimos el andamiaje vacío: que los tests tengan un proyecto donde
  compilar y fallen por la razón correcta.

  El costo, para ser honesto: si al implementar se descubre que un nombre o una
  firma de la API no encaja, hay que ajustar el test. El test-engineer lo hace,
  y el reviewer lo comprueba en el paso 6. El spec-driven tiene ese precio a
  cambio de la independencia entre quien prueba y quien implementa.

  Si prefieres otro orden, hay dos alternativas:
  - Tests después del código, que es más simple pero pierde esa independencia;
  - Híbrido: los e2e ahora, porque solo dependen de la spec, y los unitarios
    después.

  Te recomiendo seguir como está, pero es tu decisión. El agente sigue
  trabajando.

  How the pieces must behave:
  - **`validateField`** applies required, then the empty-optional skip, then
  integer-only for numbers, then the rules in order. It resolves messages per
  Q-04 and returns `Revisa este campo.` when none is usable. The first argument
  is the raw string or boolean editing value.
  - **`QuoteStore`** (sessionStorage key `quote-wizard`, entry `{version:1,
  country, step1:{values}}`):
    - Writes synchronously on every `setValue`.
    - `completeStep1` returns the typed output and sets `step1Output`, or
  returns null and leaves `step1Output` null.
    - A corrupt entry is deleted and warned about with no value. When storage
  fails, it falls back to memory with exactly one warn.
  - **`wizardStepGuard`** reads the raw stored values, not the typed output, so
  step 2 stays reachable after a reload. It fetches the config itself. Failure
  paths return `new RedirectCommand(urlTree('/<country>/datos'), { replaceUrl:
  true })`. It reads the country from `route.params`, `route.paramMap` or the
  parent route.
  - **`supportedCountryGuard`**:
    - Calls `GET /api/countries?sort=sortOrder:asc` once per page load, with a
  10 s timeout, a boundary check (`^[A-Z]{2}$`, non-empty name, `^[A-Z]{3}$`
  currency) and `console.warn` on drops.
    - Matches case-insensitively, returns `false` for an unknown code or a
  failed or timed-out list, and returns `RedirectCommand('/co/datos',
  {replaceUrl:true})` for `CO`.
    - The unknown-country page, not the guard, shows the load error.
  - **Wire format the tests feed the parser** (it is the §7.1 contract,
  flattened by Strapi 5):
    - The form-field request is `GET
  /api/form-fields?filters[country][code][$eq]=<CODE>&…`, with an upper-case
  code taken from the loaded content.
    - Items carry `key, label, type, isRequired, helpText, placeholder,
  errorMessage, requiredMessage, sortOrder`, plus
  `options[{value,label,sortOrder}]` and `rules[{kind,
  value|years|maxYearsOld|maxYearsAhead, message}]`.
    - Absent optionals arrive as `null`, and extra attributes (`id`,
  `documentId`, `__component`) must be ignored.
    - The parser output must have no nulls and no extra properties.
  - **Page DOM contract** (derived from §8 and ADR-0004):
    - Every control has a `<label>` bound by `for` or by nesting. The required
  marker `*` may sit inside the label.
    - Errors are `role="alert"` and are linked through `aria-describedby`. Help
  text is also in `aria-describedby`.
    - `aria-invalid="true"` marks invalid controls. Required controls are
  exposed through `required` or `aria-required`.
    - The `<h1>` is `Tus datos y los de tu vehículo` and is focusable, with
  `tabindex=-1`. The page shows `Cargando formulario…` inside
  `aria-busy="true"`.
    - The select prompt is `<option value="" disabled>Selecciona una
  opción</option>`, selected by default.
    - "Reintentar" receives focus on the error states.
    - The step 2 route renders nothing: no heading, no control, no button.

  ## 5. Ambiguities and risks

  1. **Rule component wire shape.** §7.1 gives `value` as a number for most
  kinds and as a string for `pattern`. A Strapi component cannot hold both in
  one attribute, so the strapi-developer must flatten it into the §7.1 logical
  shape. The tests assume that logical shape with `null` for the unused
  parameters. If the model differs, change the tests and the spec together.
  2. **Required marker format.** Tests strip `*` from labels and e2e accepts a
  trailing `*` or `(obligatorio)`. Another format, such as "Placa (requerido)",
  breaks `getByLabel`. A decision is needed.
  3. **Select prompt.** "Non-selectable prompt" is asserted as `disabled` with
  value `''` and selected by default.
  4. **Case redirect mechanism.** ADR-0001 says "redirect to canonical lower
  case with `replaceUrl`" but not how. I test it as a `RedirectCommand` returned
  by `canMatch`, rebuilt from the segments.
  5. **Focus on the step 1 heading.** §8 says "focus on the step 1 heading" for
  "Back to step 1". The tests assert it only after browser back, not on first
  arrival.
  6. **Whitespace-only optional field.** I assume it counts as empty and skips
  the rules, which is consistent with `toOutput` giving `null`. The spec only
  says "empty". Whether a pattern runs on the trimmed value is not specified,
  and I did not test it.
  7. **Keyboard e2e.**
     - Arrow keys on a closed select behave per platform: it is fine on Linux
  and in headless runs, but macOS Chrome may open the popup.
     - The date control needs `locale: 'en-US'` (set in the test) for
  month-day-year typing.
     - Chromium may add a tab stop for the date picker icon. The helper allows
  up to 4 Tab presses per field and fails if another field gets focus first.
  8. **Compose frontend port.** ADR-0002 does not fix it. I defaulted to `8080`.
  T-19 should publish 8080 or the runner sets `E2E_BASE_URL`.
  9. **AC-03 relation syntax.** The write test uses `country:
  {connect:[documentId]}` on `POST /api/form-fields`. That is unverified until
  the content type exists.

  - **No new dependency is required.**
  - **Action for the orchestrator, plumbing:** `frontend/tsconfig.app.json`
  compiles `src/testing/**`, which breaks `ng build` once production modules
  exist. Today it already reports errors there. Add `"src/testing/**"` to its
  `exclude`. I cannot edit it.
  - **Optional:** `@types/node` is absent from `frontend/` devDependencies, so
  `tsc` over `e2e/` needs types from elsewhere. I used the backend's. Playwright

  - **For the AC-03 test:** `STRAPI_ADMIN_EMAIL` and `STRAPI_ADMIN_PASSWORD`

  - **Not mine:** `git status` shows modifications to `CLAUDE.md` and
  `.claude/skills/review-checklist/SKILL.md`. I did not touch them.
  - **Hook note:** a Bash hook blocks any command that mentions `.env`. The e2e
  env helper therefore only uses it inside file content.
