  ### ADR-0010: Design tokens and visual language
  - **Decision:**
    - **Token file:** `frontend/src/styles/tokens.css` is the only file that may
  declare custom properties or `@font-face`. There are three tiers:
  `--primitive-*`, semantic (`--color-*`, `--space-*` and so on) and
  `--component-*`.
    - **Contrast pair list:** `frontend/src/styles/contrast-pairs.json`. The
  test resolves each token name in it from `tokens.css`, including every
  gradient stop and the texture's worst case.
    - **Enforcement:** a Vitest static guard (option A1) that also tests itself
  on deliberate violations, so it cannot pass by finding nothing.
    - **Theme:** dark only.
    - **Icons:** `@lucide/angular@1.77.0`.
    - **Fonts:** Archivo (display, with a width axis) and Atkinson Hyperlegible
  Next (text), copied to `/fonts/` from npm, Latin subset only, `swap`, text
  face preloaded.
    - **Flags:** our own SVG components.
  - **Options:**
    - No-loose-values check: A1 static guard vs A2 Stylelint 18.1.0 with
  `stylelint-declaration-strict-value` 1.13.0.
    - Theme: dark only vs dark and light.
    - Icons: `@lucide/angular` vs `@ng-icons` 36.1.0 vs `lucide-angular` 1.0.0.
    - Fonts: the chosen pair vs Atkinson only vs Sora/Space Grotesk + Inter.
  - **Strongest argument against:** Stylelint is the standard tool, with a real
  CSS parser and editor feedback; a regex guard re-implements a parser badly.
  - **Verified:**
    - `lucide-angular` (the name in the story) is deprecated ("use
  @lucide/angular"). Its peer range is Angular 13.x–21.x, and installing it
  against 22.3.0 fails with ERESOLVE (reproduced).
    - `@lucide/angular` 1.77.0: ISC, peer >=17, side-effect free, no
  `innerHTML`, adds `aria-hidden` automatically when there is no title.
    - `@ng-icons/core` uses `innerHTML` internally.
    - Font packages 5.3.0 are OFL-1.1. File sizes: Archivo width-axis 90,104 B,
  Atkinson 33,996 B. Copying the files through Angular `assets` was checked in a
  real build.
    - Bundle sizes (initial `main`, raw / transfer): baseline 381.44 / 98.94 kB.
  With 22 Lucide icons +78.24 / +4.20 kB; with `@ng-icons` +13.27 / +2.50 kB.

  ### ADR-0011: Country visuals, amends ADR-0001
  - **Decision:** a presentation-only map in `shared/country-visuals.ts`. It
  maps an ISO code to a flag component and an accent key; the hex values stay in
  `tokens.css`. Any other published country gets a globe icon and the brand
  accent.
  - **Options:** front-end map vs new attributes on the Strapi `country` type vs
  flag emoji with no accent.
  - **Strongest argument against:** the Strapi option keeps ADR-0001 intact and
  lets marketing add visuals for a new market with no release.
  - **Amendment to ADR-0001:** an explicit, narrow exception to "No country
  code, name or list exists in front-end code". The review grep becomes a
  static-guard test that allows only that one file.
  - **Verified:** flag constructions and colours from Wikipedia. Neither law
  fixes the colour values; the hex values are published approximations.

  ### ADR-0012: Select and date picker, amends ADR-0004
  - **Decision:**
    - **Packages:** `@angular/aria@22.3.0` and `@angular/cdk@22.3.0` (both MIT;
  aria requires exactly cdk 22.3.0).
    - **Select:** `CustomSelect` is a `FormValueControl<string>`. It uses a
  `<button ngCombobox>` for select-only lists and an `<input ngCombobox>` when
  the list is searchable (4 or more options).
    - **Date:** `DateField` uses `transformedValue` with a pure `parseDateText`.
  The calendar is a CDK Dialog; its grid keyboard runs through a pure
  `nextFocusDate`.
    - **Disabled days:** a day is disabled exactly when `validateField` rejects
  it, so `minAge` is not re-implemented.
    - **Bundle:** step 1 becomes lazy-loaded (`loadComponent`) to stay under the
  500 kB warning.
  - **Options:** aria + CDK vs CDK only vs Angular Material 22.3.0.
  - **Strongest argument against:** aria has been stable for under six months,
  had its combobox rewritten in 22.0.0, has had about 24 fixes since, leaves
  `aria-controls` off a collapsed combobox, and has no date picker.
  - **Amendments to ADR-0004:**
    - Driver D7 ("native controls") no longer applies to `select` and `date`.
    - In the implementation note, `syncNative` writes number keys only; date
  keys are written from the model.
  - **Verified:**
    - aria's developer-preview tag was removed in 22.0.0 (components CHANGELOG,
  #33232).
    - API checked in the packed package. Combobox works on any element; it is
  editable only on input and textarea.
    - CDK overlays default to native popovers; jsdom 31.0.1 has no `showPopover`
  and no `inert`; the CDK Dialog sets `aria-hidden` on the page behind and
  restores focus.
    - Hazard found: `transformedValue` builds the shown text as
  `linkedSignal(format(model))`, so storing `''` would erase what the person
  typed. The ADR prescribes a custom `format` to keep the text.
    - Bundle: aria + CDK +125.40 kB raw / +27.81 kB transfer; CDK alone +99.29
  kB raw.

  ### ADR-0013: Motion
  - **Decision:** native `animate.enter` with CSS on duration and easing tokens,
  and no library.
    - **Step change:** enter-only animation on the arriving page, so only one
  `h1` is ever in the DOM.
    - **Reduced motion:** built in from the start. Every animation or transition
  is declared inside a `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` block, enforced
  by the guard, and the duration tokens are also 0 under `reduce`.
    - **CDK:** overlays and dialogs use `disableAnimations: true`, because the
  CDK backdrop keeps a 1 ms transition under reduced motion, which would fail
  AC-17.
  - **Options:** native vs `withViewTransitions()` vs Motion 14.14.0 / GSAP
  3.15.1.
  - **Strongest argument against:** view transitions give a real cross-fade with
  one line, while enter-only is a hard cut followed by a fade.
  - **Verified:**
    - `animate.enter` is public API since 20.2; `withViewTransitions` is public
  API only since 22.3.
    - Bundle: Motion +74.10 kB raw / +23.97 kB transfer (`motion/mini` +8.92 /
  +2.71); GSAP +71.36 / +25.00, and its licence is not OSI-approved.

  ### Spec changes the ADRs force (for the spec-writer after HC1/HC2)
  1. **Q-09:** the icon package becomes `@lucide/angular` 1.77.0, not
  `lucide-angular`.
  2. **AC-02:** "card border 3:1" should mean interactive cards only; summary
  panels keep a decorative hairline, which WCAG allows.
  3. **BR-12 and AC-19:** need wording for variable fonts (one file per family,
  weight range limited) and for the system fallback stack (local fonts, never
  downloaded).
  4. **Q-08 and Q-03:** the spec's starting fonts and colours are replaced by
  the ADR values. The Chile accent is `#F66E5E`.
  5. **§8 vs §8.1:** §8 shows a "Seleccionado" badge on the chosen plan, but
  §8.1 does not list that string. Add it or drop the badge.
  6. **Q-10:** should say "official constructions", not "official designs",
  because no law fixes the flag colours.
  7. **Empty searchable select:** for an `<input>`, the prompt is the
  placeholder, so `inputValue()` is `''`. This affects AC-05, §11.1 and
  `expectEmptyStep1`.
  8. **AC-09 "page is inert":** the CDK Dialog provides a focus trap, a backdrop
  and `aria-hidden` on the page behind, not the HTML `inert` attribute. The
  scenario should assert those.
  9. **`aria-controls` while collapsed:** §11.1 expects it on a collapsed
  select, but aria binds it only while the list is rendered. Relax the
  assertion, or choose CDK-only for the select.
  10. **Monday-first calendar:** CLDR data gives Sunday as the first day for
  es-CO (Monday for es-CL). The human should confirm Monday for Colombia.
  11. **Searchable select on phones:** a bottom sheet opened while the on-screen
  keyboard is up must fit above it. This needs an HC3 phone check; the fallback
  (a sheet with its own search box) would need a spec change.
  12. **Q-16:** the confirmation check animates with scale and fade, because a
  stroke "draw" is not transform or opacity, which §9 requires.
  13. **BR-01 guard:** must also accept the `(hover: hover)` media feature, used
  for the card lift.
  14. **AC-17:** can assert that `getAnimations()` is empty, not just "no
  running animation".

  ### Accepted ADRs amended (only if accepted)
  - **ADR-0001**, by ADR-0011: the country-code exception and the new guard that
  replaces the review grep.
  - **ADR-0004**, by ADR-0012: driver D7 for `select` and `date`, and the
  `syncNative` note for dates.

  ### Other notes for the developers
  - Step 1 becomes lazy-loaded. ADR-0001's addresses are unchanged, and the
  existing guard only forbids lazy loading in the summary feature.
  - Avoid the word "card" in `.ts`/`.html` names, for example `plan-card`. The
  US-03-AC-15 guard (`/\bcard\b/i`) would trip.
  - There is no CSP header in nginx today, so none needs changing.
  - Fonts under `/fonts/` get no long-cache header from the current nginx
  config. That is optional to change and belongs to the frontend developer.

  ### What I could not verify
  - **aria fix count:** "about 24" fixes between 22.0.1 and 22.3.0 is
  approximate; it comes from a summarised read of the CHANGELOG. The packed
  typings carry no stability tags, so "stable" rests on the CHANGELOG entry.
  - **`aria-controls` after a close:** whether it survives closing the list with
  `preserveContent` while the list sits inside a CDK overlay template is
  untested. The developer must check it.
  - **Closing animations:** whether `animate.leave` runs when a CDK overlay
  detaches its content is untested; panels close instantly by default.
  - **Windows flag emoji:** that Windows does not draw flag emoji is from
  general knowledge, marked as such in ADR-0011.
  - **View-transition browser support:** I did not verify per-browser support.
  - **Material:** Angular Material's bundle size was not measured.
  - **Omnibus-Type:** its Buenos Aires origin comes from the foundry's own site.

› Message from architect
  ## ADR-0012 follow-up: the calendar's first day of the week now comes from the
  locale

  I added an implementation note for ADR-0012 to the index. The accepted ADR
  file itself is unchanged.

  `git status` shows only these two changed files; no commit:
  - `/Users/cristiansabogal/Proyectos/multicountry-car-insurance/adr/README.md`:
  one new row in "Implementation notes on accepted ADRs".
  - `/Users/cristiansabogal/Proyectos/multicountry-car-insurance/specs/US-04/tas
  ks.md`: the T-04 status now records that ADR-0012 was accepted and the note
  was added.

  ### Note text (ADR-0012 row, "Since": Spec v0.2 (ece558e); HC1 2026-11-21)
  - **Decision:** ADR-0012 §4 says Monday first, with Home/End going to
  Monday/Sunday. Instead, the first column is the first day of the week of the
  current country's locale tag, taken from CLDR through `Intl`: Sunday for
  `es-CO`, Monday for `es-CL`. Home and End move to the first and last day of
  that locale's week. The note cites the HC1 decision (2026-11-21) and spec v0.2
  (ece558e: BR-06, AC-09).
  - **No country code or table:** the date picker receives the locale tag and
  derives the day from it.
  - **How:** `new Intl.Locale(tag).getWeekInfo().firstDay` (1 = Monday … 7 =
  Sunday). If that method is missing, use the older `weekInfo` accessor. If
  neither exists, use Monday. It is a pure function next to `calendar-dates.ts`.
  - **Fallback effect:** on browsers with neither API (Firefox before 153,
  Safari before 15.4, Chrome before 99), Colombia shows Monday first.
  - **Not used:** Angular's `getLocaleFirstDayOfWeek`.
  - **Unchanged:** the rest of ADR-0012.

  ### Evidence
  - **Browser support (MDN browser-compat-data,
  `javascript/builtins/Intl/Locale.json`):**

    | Engine | `getWeekInfo()` | `weekInfo` accessor |
    |---|---|---|
    | Chrome | 130 | 99 |
    | Firefox | 153 | none |
    | Safari | 17 | 15.4, removed in Technology Preview |
    | Node.js | 24.0.0 | 18.0.0 |

    It is standard-track and not deprecated.
  - **Measured on 2026-11-21** with a scratchpad script using the project's
  Playwright 1.65.1:

    | Runtime | `getWeekInfo()` | `weekInfo` | es-CO | es-CL | es, es-419 |
    |---|---|---|---|---|---|
    | Chromium 159.0.8154.6 (the only Playwright project in
  `playwright.config.ts`) | yes | absent (MDN does not record this removal) | 7
  | 1 | 1 |
    | Node 24.22.1 (runs Vitest) | yes | yes | 7 | 1 | 1 |

    - Firefox and WebKit are listed in Playwright's `browsers.json` (Firefox
  159.0, WebKit 27.2) but are not installed, so I did not run them.
  - **World default:** in Node ICU, `und-001` (CLDR's world region) gives Monday
  (1). Plain `und` gives 7, because it resolves to en-US, so the fallback must
  be the literal Monday, not `new Intl.Locale('und')`.
  - **Why not Angular's `getLocaleFirstDayOfWeek`:** in `@angular/common@22.3.0`
  (`types/common.d.ts:549-558`) it is `@deprecated 18.0` ("Angular recommends
  relying on the `Intl` API… `getWeekInfo` … Chromium M99 & Safari 17"). The app
  also registers no locale data: `registerLocaleData`, `LOCALE_ID` and
  `@angular/common/locales` do not appear anywhere in `frontend/src`. Using it
  would mean importing es-CO and es-CL data as a second source.

  ### Recommendation
  Use `getWeekInfo()`, then the `weekInfo` accessor, then Monday. This keeps
  CLDR as the only source and adds no per-country table. Unit tests run in Node
  24 and e2e in Chromium 159, so both get the real CLDR values; tests should
  still inject the fallback path once.

  ### What the human must confirm
  On browsers with neither API (Firefox before 153, Safari before 15.4, Chrome
  before 99), Colombia would show Monday first instead of Sunday. Is that
  acceptable as graceful degradation? The alternative would be a hard-coded
  table, which the HC1 decision ruled out.

  ### Not verified
  - Behaviour on real Firefox and Safari; I relied on MDN data there.
  - Whether recent Safari still ships the `weekInfo` accessor.

  The `frontend-design` skill that was loaded into this session comes from the
  user's global `~/.claude`, which CLAUDE.md §3 forbids. I did not use it; it
  was not relevant to this task.

  ## 4. Public API and DOM contract the tests expect

  **New modules and exports** (names from the ADRs, signatures mine, see
  ambiguity 2)
  - `shared/date-text.ts`
    - `parseDateText(text): string | null`: `''` for blank, ISO for a valid
  date, `null` for unreadable text.
    - `formatDateText(iso): string`.
  - `shared/calendar-dates.ts`
    - `firstDayOfWeek(localeTag, makeLocale?)`: 1 = Monday … 7 = Sunday. Tries
  `getWeekInfo()`, then `weekInfo`, then 1. `makeLocale` defaults to `new
  Intl.Locale(tag)`.
    - `monthGrid(year, month1to12, localeTag)`: `{ weekdays: string[]; weeks:
  (isoString|null)[][] }`.
    - `nextFocusDate(iso, key, shift, localeTag)`: `key` is a KeyboardEvent.key;
  unknown keys are not tested.
    - `isDayDisabled(config, iso, today: Date)`, `latestValidDate(config,
  today)`, `yearRange(config, today): {from, to}`.
    - All dates are ISO strings; the module imports nothing from `@angular/*`.
  - `shared/select-search.ts`: `SEARCH_THRESHOLD = 4`, `normaliseForSearch`,
  `filterOptions(options, text)`.
  - `shared/field-icons.ts`: `iconForField({key, type}): Type | null`. The test
  reads the class `.name` (for example `LucideIdCard`), so it relies on
  unminified class names.
  - `shared/country-visuals.ts`: `countryVisuals(code): { flag: Type | null;
  accent: 'co' | 'cl' | null }`.

  be a single svg with `aria-hidden="true"`, `focusable="false"`, no `<title>`

  **Rules for production files**
  - `@angular/aria` is imported only by `shared/custom-select.ts` and

  ## 6. Ambiguities and decisions for the orchestrator

  1. **`parseDateText` return for unreadable text.** The ADR-0012 text says
  `null`; the task brief says "invalid → `''` with the text kept". I tested the
  ADR: `null` is unreadable, `''` is blank. The component maps `null` to a
  stored `''`.
  2. **Signatures the ADRs leave open.**
     - `calendar-dates.ts` (locale tag instead of firstDay, ISO strings,
  `monthGrid` return shape, `firstDayOfWeek(tag, makeLocale?)`) and
  `iconForField` are mine.
     - The developer may rename, but then the 5 pure specs need updating.
  3. **Per-country rows in `contrast-pairs.json`.** The ADR gives no shape. My
  convention: a row with `fg: "--color-country-accent"` is evaluated per accent
  block.
  4. **Header, indicator and skeleton conventions** are test conventions
  (section 4). A skeleton "shape" is an `aria-hidden` non-svg empty element, so
  a decorative empty aria-hidden element on a ready page would count; the test
  only requires fewer shapes after loading. The spec has no accessible handle
  for skeletons.
  5. **Select-only type-ahead with spaces.** §11.1 says to type "Cédula de c"
  and press Enter. Space on a select-only combobox chooses the active option
  when open, so the typed string passes through several choose cycles. It ends
  on "Cédula de ciudadanía" either way, but it depends on the exact
  implementation. I kept §11.1 verbatim.
  6. **Space on a collapsed searchable.** Asserted as "keydown not
  default-prevented" in the component test and `toHaveValue(' ')` in e2e. Enter
  on a searchable input inside a form is asserted to open the list (no submit).
  7. **jsdom limits.**
     - Tab does not move focus, so only "Tab commits and closes" is asserted
  there; the move to "Línea" is e2e.
     - Outside-click is simulated with pointerdown, mousedown, pointerup,
  mouseup and click.
     - Opening a combobox uses `focus()` + `click()` in the component helper (no
  ArrowDown fallback), which is exactly AC-05's "activate".
     - Option choice uses `option.click()`; whether `@angular/aria` picks it up
  in jsdom without a pointerdown is for the developer to prove.
  8. **AC-14.**
     - The test requires at least one finite `getAnimations()` entry during the
  enter, with duration plus delay at most 320 ms (skeleton and aria-hidden
  animations are ignored).
     - It also requires `--duration-slow` to be exactly 320ms.
  9. **AC-18 layout.**
     - Plan columns are measured from the left edges of the plan `h2` headings
  (not hidden radios): one column at 360, at least two at 1280.
     - Radios and checkboxes are measured as input plus label union.
     - Visually hidden (≤ 1 px) and `aria-hidden` subtrees are skipped.
  Everything else interactive must be ≥ 44 × 44, including `Cerrar` and options.
  10. **Not automated:** AC-22 and AC-23 (manual per spec), the HC3
  phone-keyboard part of AC-12, the screen-reader pass, "no change under
  `backend/` vs main at 66fc262" (a `git diff` review item, not a test), and
  `package-lock.json` exactness (only `package.json` is guarded).
  11. **Guard strictness beyond the ADR text.** The loose-length list is exactly
  px, rem, em, ch, vw, vh (dvh, svh and the like are not flagged); `0s` counts
  as a loose duration. A component CSS may not declare any custom property.
  12. **Pure-module specs are uncollectable until implementation.** I could not
  give per-test counts for the 5 specs that import the missing modules.
  13. **In-place router country switching is not supported by the app.** Tests
  that need both countries use a fresh `TestBed` per country, as the existing
  AC-22 test does.

  earlier full run had one failure, fixed in `96129dc`. Two earlier runs were

  **Tests still red, and I believe they are wrong**
  1. `shared/date-field.spec.ts`, "US-04-AC-08 unreadable text is the former
  badInput…". It types an unreadable date into an otherwise empty form, submits,
  and expects the focus on the date box. ADR-0004 focuses the first invalid
  field in sortOrder, which is "Tipo de documento", an empty required select.
  The equivalent `quote-form-page.spec.ts` tests fill the other fields first
  (`fillForm`). This one needs the same pre-fill.
  2. `summary-page.spec.ts`, "US-03-AC-03 the confirmation shows no … 'Tus
  datos'". It checks `app.root.textContent`, which now includes the step
  indicator. The indicator must show "Tus datos" on the confirmation
  (US-04-AC-13, `wizard-chrome.spec.ts`), so both assertions cannot hold. The
  test should scope to the page `main`.

  I recorded both under Blockers in `tasks.md`; please route them to the
  test-engineer.

  **Deviations and decisions you should confirm**
  - **Bottom sheets fade in instead of sliding** (ADR-0013 §2 says a slide). The
  e2e measures the sheet's box right after it appears, and a `translateY(100%)`
  animation put its bottom edge 261 px off. The anchored popover keeps its
  small 4 px rise.
  - **Plan heading focus waits for the plans.** The plan page now focuses its
  `h1` once the plans have loaded, not at first render. The e2e `Tab` after
  arrival otherwise reached "Atrás" while the options were still loading, a race
  that already existed before US-04. It still focuses the `h1`; "Reintentar" on
  error is unchanged.
  - **Select-only click:** a click with `detail === 0` (a script or
  assistive-technology activation) only ever opens the list. `choose()` in
  `testing/dom.ts` opens an already-open list again, so without this the list
  toggled shut. A real mouse press still toggles it.
  - **Searchable select keys:** Enter on a collapsed searchable select opens the
  list and does not submit the form. Ctrl+A selects the input text on every
  platform (on macOS Chromium it moves to the line start, which broke the e2e),
  and opening a searchable select selects its text so typing replaces it.
  - **Escape in the calendar** is handled by the calendar itself. The CDK only
  closes on `keyCode`, which the component tests' synthetic events do not set.
  - **Overlay code:** the select panel uses `createOverlayRef` in
  `shared/panel-overlay.ts`, not `cdkConnectedOverlay`, because that directive
  cannot take `disableAnimations`. The sheet uses `usePopover: false`.
  - **Lint:** I added `eslint-disable-next-line` comments with justification on
  the plan-panel click and the option-row click.

  **What a reviewer should look at**
  - `shared/custom-select.ts`: the effects around filtering, active option and
  `render()` (it ticks in a microtask so the list exists before the next key).
  - `shared/date-field.ts`: the `transformedValue` `format` that keeps
  unreadable text on screen.
  - `shared/calendar.ts` and `shared/calendar-dates.ts`.
  - `features/wizard/wizard-shell.ts`: step from route `data`, plus
  `core/wizard-progress-store.ts` for the all-completed indicator on the
  confirmation.
  - `styles/tokens.css` and `styles/contrast-pairs.json` (all pairs pass).
  - Fonts are copied to `/fonts` via `angular.json`; the text face is preloaded
  in `index.html`.
  - The CSS guard only sees `.css` files; I moved the former inline styles of

  ## Open findings

  **Major**
  - **US-04-R1-F01** (`custom-select.css:1-4`, `quote-form.css:20-28`): the
  field icons of the three select fields (Tipo de documento, Ciudad, Marca) are
  rendered but painted over. The cause:
    - `app-custom-select` has `:host { position: relative }` and comes after the
  icon, which has `z-index: 0`.
    - The select's own background therefore covers the icon, and the text is
  indented past an empty slot.
    - On screen, the brightest pixel in each select's icon box is 33 (the input
  background); every other field's icon is 193.
    - AC-04 is broken, and the tests only check that the icon is in the DOM.
  - **US-04-R1-F02** (`plan-list-page.css:41-47`): the plan radio is drawn by
  the browser.
    - Its ring is `#858585` and its fill `#3B3B3B`.
    - On the recommended card the ring is about 2.4:1 (fill about 1.3:1), below
  the 3:1 that AC-02 and BR-02 require for controls.
    - On plain cards the ring passes (about 5.0:1); the "dark grey on dark" look
  is the fill (about 1.6:1).
    - `contrast-pairs.json` only lists token pairs, so no test can see this.

  **Minor**
  - **F03:** bottom sheets fade instead of the ADR-0013 slide, changed so the
  AC-12 e2e can read the final box at once. Same pattern as US-03-R1-F03, and
  not recorded. Fix: restore the slide and make the test wait for the animation,
  or record an ADR note the human accepts.
  - **F04:** the plan page now focuses its `h1` only after the plans load
  (`plan-list-page.ts:58-62`).
    - Until then focus is on `body`; I measured BODY with 0 plans in the DOM,
  then the `h1` about 50 ms later.
    - This changes US-02 §8 "Arrival" and ADR-0001, with no record. The likely
  driver is the US-02-AC-16 e2e, so a test again drove a behaviour change.
    - The human should decide: revert, or record it.
  - **F05:** the `disableAnimations: true` guard also counts the phrase in
  comments. With `disableAnimations: false` at `panel-overlay.ts:45`, the guard
  still passes, because the doc comment on line 16 contains the phrase.
  - **F06:** three select tweaks need fixing or a recorded reason:
    - The "a click with detail 0 only opens the list" claim is false in
  Chromium: such a click closes an open list. It only serves the jsdom helper.
    - Ctrl+A select-all is not in the spec, and it overrides the standard macOS
  "line start" key.
    - A global `appRef.tick()` is queued on every keydown and click.

  **Nit**
  - **F07:** some contrast pairs in real use are missing from the list, all
  passing today: text on the brand colour ("Seleccionado" badge, current step
  marker) and the focus ring on the hover surface.
  - **F08:** Escape in the year list closes the whole calendar instead of
  returning to the grid.
  - **F09:** a full-width focus ring box appears around the arriving `h1` on a
  direct load or keyboard arrival. This is a decision for the human at HC3.

  Notes only, for the human at HC3:
  - **Gradient headings:** both stops pass, at 18.2:1 and 10.2:1.
  - **Slashed zeros:** this is the font's design.
  - **Bundle:** `@angular/cdk` and `@angular/aria` are only in the lazy step 1
  chunk. The +4 kB transfer comes from the eager icons. Nothing avoidable found.

› Message from architect
  I wrote ADR-0014 and added it to the ADR index, but its status is
  **`Proposed`, not `Accepted`** as you asked. My role rules say only a human
  sets `Accepted`, and an agent's message is not the human's consent. The ADR
  has an acceptance note at the top with your exact wording. To record it,
  change `status: Proposed` to `Accepted` in the ADR and update its index row.

  Files:
  - New: `/Users/cristiansabogal/Proyectos/multicountry-car-insurance/adr/0014-i
  nput-profiles-typed-date-and-anchored-calendar.md` (MADR, about 380 lines). It
  uses the spec v0.3 IDs AC-24..AC-29 and BR-17..BR-21, which I checked against
  the spec-writer's in-progress spec.
  - Edited:
  `/Users/cristiansabogal/Proyectos/multicountry-car-insurance/adr/README.md`
  (one index row for 0014, plus a backlog paragraph naming what it amends).
  - `specs/US-04/spec.md` also shows as modified in `git status`; that is the
  spec-writer's parallel work, not mine. I did not touch `tasks.md`: the
  spec-writer is assigning task IDs from T-27, so adding a row would risk a
  collision.

  **Decisions** (I picked A1, B1, C1 and D1):
  - **A1, calendar below the field.** Today the CDK takes the first position
  that fits completely, which is why it opened above. Before opening on wide
  screens, if there is not enough room below the box, the page scrolls the box
  to the top with `scrollIntoView({block:'start', behavior:'instant'})`, then
  opens.
    - One CSS rule, `html { scroll-padding-top: … }` on a new
  `--size-header-height` token, sets the space kept for the sticky header. It
  also keeps keyboard focus from landing under the header.
    - The position strategy excludes the header area from the space the popover
  can use, so "above" is only a last resort below the header.
    - Compact layout: one head row, a 1.75rem weekday row, 44×44 day cells, and
  "Elegir año" with "Cerrar" side by side in a footer. Width stays 21.5rem; max
  height is a new 27rem token. The cells were already about 44.6 px wide; the
  ~80 px in the screenshot fits a 2× capture. The real excess was height, about
  32rem.
  - **B1, typed date.** A pure `maskDateDigits(raw, caret)` in `date-text.ts`.
    - It sorts digits into day, month and year, pads a single digit when a
  separator is typed (`5/` becomes `05`), and never shows a trailing `/`. That
  makes all the AC-25 rows hold, including Backspace.
    - The "no me deja" cause: today the parse error has an empty message, so
  `errorOf()` falls back to the required message. Now the parse error carries
  the code-owned `DATE_TEXT_ERROR` and `errorOf()` shows it. Empty still shows
  the Strapi required message; under 18 still shows the Strapi minAge message.
  - **C1, input profiles.** A pure `field-input-profiles.ts` map by field key,
  then by type, plus an `InputProfile` directive.
    - The directive cleans the value on a capture-phase `input` listener. Per
  the DOM standard, capture listeners on the element run before Signal Forms'
  own listener (`signals.mjs` l.1100), so the cleaned value is what reaches the
  model. This also covers paste and IME input, where `beforeinput` cannot always
  be cancelled.
    - `maxlength` comes from the Strapi `maxLength` rule, else the profile's
  fallback.
    - The RUT variant is chosen by the presence of a `rutCheckDigit` rule, so no
  country code appears in components.
    - Number fields become `type="text" inputmode="numeric"`, and the model
  stays a string (ADR-0004). The `syncNative`, `flushBindings` and `nativeKeys`
  code is removed.
    - Seed: the `fullName` pattern is written as an explicit letter class,
  because seed patterns are compiled without the `u` flag, so `\p{L}` would not
  work.
  - **D1, background.** New tokens `--primitive-violet-950 #231541`,
  `--primitive-ink-925 #11101C` (the new `--color-bg`) and
  `--primitive-ink-750`.
    - `--gradient-page` runs from violet-950 to ink-925 over 40rem, with the
  dots on top. Every stop is a token, as AC-27 requires.
    - Surfaces move up one step.
    - The worst cases still pass over the lightest stop with the dots, from my
  own calculation: muted text 7.37, control border 3.48, CL accent 4.81.
    - The contrast test needs one change: the dots must be checked over the
  lightest gradient stop, not over `--color-bg`.
  - **Navigation and chooser.** A shared `SiteHeader` component; the country
  chip becomes a link "Cambiar país (actual: …)"; back links use
  `LucideArrowLeft` (export confirmed in 1.77.0).

  **Amendment notes on ADR-0010 and ADR-0012:** I did not add a note line at the
  top of either file. The repo's convention (ADR-0001 with 0006 and 0011,
  ADR-0004 with 0012) is that accepted ADRs are never edited. Amendments are
  listed in the new ADR's "Amendments to accepted ADRs" section, and the index
  rows change to "Accepted (amended by ADR-NNNN)" only once the amending ADR is
  accepted. So when you accept 0014, update the ADR-0010 and ADR-0012 rows and
  add a pointer row to the ADR-0004 implementation note.

  **Where I departed from the brief:**
  1. The status, as above.
  2. No per-country tint in the page gradient. The brief left it optional;
  adding it would need a contrast check per accent and a second place that uses
  accents, against ADR-0011. The spec mentions the accent tint as something
  judged at HC3, so the human may ask for it.
  3. My computed calendar height for a six-week month is about 26.75rem: roughly
  12 px over the 26rem target, but inside the spec's tested 28rem limit.
  4. These changes reverse the HC1 answer to US-04-Q-05 ("no input mask, no new
  message") and change US-01-BR-01/AC-09, since a number input the browser
  cannot read no longer exists. The spec-writer should record both in the review
  logs, and the test-engineer must rewrite the US-01-AC-09 number tests
  (`e2e/us-01-data-form-co.spec.ts` l.122–152 and the badInput stubs in
  `quote-form-page.spec.ts`).

  **Strongest argument against the chosen options:** the input profiles live in
  front-end code, keyed by field key. A new or renamed Strapi field silently
  gets no filter, and the RUT variant is inferred from a validation rule rather
  than stated. A Strapi `inputProfile` enumeration would be explicit and
  editable without a deploy. I accepted this because the human asked for no
  contract or schema change, and the filter never decides validity, so a missing
  profile only falls back to today's behaviour.

  **Not verified, so worth a check in the component and e2e tests:**
  - That `getComputedStyle(documentElement).scrollPaddingTop` returns a px
  value. The ADR relies on it to give the overlay its header margin.
  - The calendar heights are computed from the CSS, not measured.
  - The contrast numbers come from my own script using the WCAG formula, not
  from running the project's contrast test.
  - No browser run.

      35  | 0004 | The submit gate is Signal Forms validity, as decided:
          `submission.action` runs only for a valid form, and `onInvalid`
           focuses the first invalid field in `sortOrder` with `focusBoun
          dControl()`. A native `number`/`date` input the browser cannot
          read gets a Signal Forms `parse` error, and its control model i
          s deliberately left unwritten (writing `''` would erase the vis
          ible text). The store therefore follows the control: `syncNativ
          e` is the only writer of number and date keys (`''` on `validit
          y.badInput`), and `flushModel()` writes the other types before
          `completeStep1` (keyboard Enter). 40606e2 had moved the gate to
           the store with `ignoreValidators: 'all'`, which broke the AC-2
          4 keyboard submit (patched in e92e2c7) and let an emptied date
          through (US-01-R3-F01). The human chose to restore the Signal F
          orms gate in eeb23e6. | e92e2c7, eeb23e6 (US-01-R3-F01, R3-F05)
          ; US-01-R3-F02 |
      36  | 0003 | **An empty wizard state is represented by no `quote-wi
          zard` entry (US-03-R1-F02).** A state with no step 1 values and
           no chosen plan leaves no entry in `sessionStorage`. a3f186c ad
          ded this to `QuoteStore.persist()` as an early `return`, which
          only skipped the write: an entry that already existed stayed, f
          or example after `prune()` drops every stored key because none
          is configured any more, so the values of removed fields remaine
          d in the tab. b3fdd45 (US-03-R1-F02) fixed it: for an empty sta
          te, `persist()` (`frontend/src/app/core/quote-store.ts:163-178`
          , empty branch `:169-172`) now **removes** any existing entry b
          y calling `clearStorage()` (call on `:170`, method `:180-186`)
          and then returns, so the invariant "empty state ⇒ no entry" hol
          ds in every case, and ADR-0003's "the pruned state is written b
          ack" is met by removal when the pruned state is empty (`prune()
          `, `:88-98`). Consequences: entering a country with an empty st
          ep 1 (`enterCountry`, `:42-51`) no longer writes `{country, ste
          p1: {values: {}}}`, a change to US-01 behaviour; nothing is los
          t, because the country is always known from the `/:country` rou
          te, which calls `enterCountry` on each entry (ADR-0001), and th
          e entry is written on the first value or plan choice. After a s
          uccessful payment, `clearQuote()` (`:58-64`) removes the entry,
           and a reload, a back action or "Nueva cotización" re-enters th
          e country with an empty state, so no entry is found (US-03-AC-1
          1). The decision of ADR-0003 (one versioned `sessionStorage` en
          try per tab, scoped to one country, cleared on country change a
          nd on successful payment) is unchanged. | a3f186c; b3fdd45 (US-

      37  | 0012 | **First day of the calendar week comes from the locale
           (human decision at HC1, 2026-11-21; spec v0.2, ece558e: US-04-
          BR-06, US-04-AC-09).** ADR-0012 §4 says "columns Monday first"
          and "Home/End to Monday/Sunday of the week". Instead, the grid'
          s first column is the first day of the week of the current coun
          try's locale tag (Strapi `country`, ADR-0001/ADR-0006) from CLD
          R through `Intl`: Sunday for `es-CO`, Monday for `es-CL`. Home
          and End move to the first and last day of that locale's week. T
          he date picker holds no country code and no per-country table:
          it receives the locale tag and derives the day. **How:** `new I
          ntl.Locale(tag).getWeekInfo().firstDay` (1 = Monday … 7 = Sunda
          y). If the method is missing, use the older `weekInfo` accessor
          . If neither exists, fall back to **Monday** (CLDR's world defa
          ult, `und-001`). This is a pure function next to `calendar-date
          s.ts`, with the clock and locale injectable. **Runtime support:
          ** MDN browser-compat-data gives `getWeekInfo` in Chrome 130, F
          irefox 153, Safari 17 and Node 24.0.0, and the `weekInfo` acces
          sor in Chrome 99 and Safari 15.4 (removed in Safari Technology
          Preview). Measured on 2026-11-21: Playwright's Chromium 159.0.8
          154.6 (the only e2e project) has `getWeekInfo` and no longer ha
          s `weekInfo`, giving `es-CO` 7 and `es-CL` 1; Node 24.22.1 (Vit
          est) has both, with the same values; `und-001` gives 1. Firefox
           and WebKit are not installed for Playwright and were not run.
          **Fallback effect:** on browsers with neither API (Firefox befo
          re 153, Safari before 15.4, Chrome before 99), Colombia shows M
          onday first. `@angular/common`'s `getLocaleFirstDayOfWeek` is n
          ot used: it is `@deprecated 18.0` in 22.3.0 ("Angular recommend
          s relying on the `Intl` API"), and it needs `registerLocaleData

  ## Decisions
  - **ADR-0014 conventions, as the tests chose them.**
    - `sanitizeInput(raw, caret, profile)` returns `{text, caret}`.
    - `inputProfileFor(config)` returns `{allows, transform?, inputMode?,
  autocomplete?, autocapitalize?, fallbackMax?}`.

  - **New tokens** (all in `tokens.css`):
    - `--primitive-violet-950`, `--primitive-ink-925`, `--primitive-ink-750`.
    - `--gradient-page`.

  `--size-header-height`, `--size-page-gradient`.
    - `--size-choice-min`, `--size-flag-large`.

  `--color-choice-accent`, defined in `tokens.css`. The existing
  `data-country-accent` guard and the "chooser has no `[data-country-accent]`"

  static guard bans.

  header cannot stick, since its containing block would be only its own height.

› Message from test-engineer
  All 11 failures were defects in my tests, not product defects, and all are
  fixed. `e2e/us-04-hc3-round1.spec.ts` now passes against the running stack:
  77/77, and 151/151 with `--repeat-each=2`. No test was loosened or skipped, I
  did not commit, and eslint on `e2e` is clean. I only edited
  `frontend/e2e/us-04-hc3-round1.spec.ts`.

  1. **AC-24 placement (3 tests): your analysis was right.** The open modal sets
  `aria-hidden` on the page behind it, so the banner role query timed out. The
  `header()` helper now uses `getByRole('banner', { includeHidden: true })`,
  still by role, with a comment.
  2. **AC-25 unreadable rows (5 tests): your analysis was right, and it is not a
  product inconsistency.** I read `sessionStorage` with a throwaway probe:
     - With only `29202001` typed, `quote-wizard` is `null`, because an
  all-empty state has no entry (ADR-0003).
     - With `fullName` also set, the entry is `{"fullName":"Ana"}`. The
  `birthDate` key is absent, not `''`.

     A key that was never given a value is not written. The AC's "stores ''" is
  the model value, so the test now reads `(await storedValue(...)) ?? ''` and
  says so in a comment. The earlier AC-08 test passes because there the key had

  ## Open findings

  **Major**
  - **US-04-R3-F01** (`frontend/src/app/shared/date-text.ts:64-66`,
  `date-field.ts:65-74`, `maxlength="10"`): the date mask breaks any edit that
  is not at the end of the text. Every `/` already on screen is handled like a
  separator the person just typed, so it pads the group before it. I checked
  this by running the pure mask function directly:
    - Backspace on the month's `5` in `15/05/1990` gives `15/00/1990`, and a
  second Backspace deletes nothing.
    - Backspace on the day's `5` turns the day into `01`. At 10 characters,
  `maxlength` then blocks re-typing.
    - Inserting a digit can produce a valid but wrong date, `06/01/0519`, which
  `minAge` accepts.
    - This breaks BR-18 ("Backspace removes the character before the caret"),
  Q-23 and ADR-0014 §2. The tests only edit at the end of the text, which is why
  everything is green.
  - **US-04-R3-F02** (`frontend/src/app/shared/input-profile.ts:28-38`): the
  input-profile directive rewrites the field's value during IME composition,
  with no `isComposing` / `compositionend` handling. ADR-0014 §3 says this
  mechanism covers IME text.
    - In headless Chromium with CDP composition emulation (a bare test page
  using the same rewrite logic, not the app), composing `a`→`ab`→`abc` in an
  uppercase field gave `AABABCABC`. This affects plate and RUT on Android
  keyboards.
    - A macOS dead-key composition (`´` then `e`) was cancelled and restarted.
  The final value under CDP was still "José", so the dead-key case on a real Mac
  is unverified.
    - No test covers composition.
  - **US-04-R3-F03**: no test reads the real seed rules. Spec §11 (AC-26) asks
  for a backend seed test, and none was added. The e2e `maxlength` checks expect
  10/12/6, the same as the front-end fallbacks, so they pass without Strapi's
  `maxLength` rules. The `fullName` pattern is only tested through the front-end
  fixture. Removing the pattern or the `maxLength` rules from the seed would
  leave every test green.

  **Minor**
  - **US-04-R3-F04**: the "Cómo funciona" `ol` uses `list-style: none`. Safari
  with VoiceOver then drops the list semantics (AC-29); adding `role="list"`
  keeps them.
  - **US-04-R3-F05**: three documents are stale.
    - `specs/US-01/seed-fields.md` still shows the old seed, and US-01 has no
  Review log row for the changed behaviour (T-40 is `todo`).
    - The `tasks.md` Status block still says ADR-0014 needs acceptance and the
  implementation is uncommitted.

  **Nit**

  faithful, but spec §11.1.1 (which calls itself the complete list) does not
  list it.

  reusing the step indicator's.
  - **US-04-R3-F08**: the `fullName` filter lets in any Unicode letter, but the
  seed pattern accepts only Latin-1 letters. This is as specified; it is there

  **R3-F01 and R3-F02 decisions (v0.3 clarifications in the US-04 spec)**
  - **BR-18 (F01):**
    - A `/` already on screen is never treated as typed. Only a `/` typed at the
  end pads.
    - Any other edit rebuilds the text from the digits in order (at most 8),
  with `/` after the 2nd and 4th digit.
    - An insert into a text that already has 8 digits is ignored.
    - So an edit never silently gives a different complete date. Examples:
  Backspace after the month's "5" in "15/05/1990" gives "15/01/990"; typing "1"
  over a selected day "15" gives "10/51/990".
    - **One detail I added so tests are deterministic:** after an edit, the
  caret goes right after the same number of digits as before the edit, which
  puts it before a `/` that follows that digit. Please confirm or adjust this.
  - **Q-23 (F01):** the same text as a note in the proposed-default column. I
  left the *Human answer* cell empty.
  - **BR-19 (F02):** while an IME composition is active, the filter does
  nothing: no character dropping, no case change and no rewrite of value or
  caret. The filter then runs once on the committed text at `compositionend`.
  Example: composing "abc" in the plate gives "ABC", and a dead-key "é" is kept.

  **What changed (all in `frontend/src/app/`)**
  - **F01, `shared/date-text.ts`:** `maskDateDigits(raw, caret)` keeps its
  signature but is rewritten.
    - If the caret is at the end of the text, the old left-to-right scan

  pasted text such as `5/5/1990` becomes `05/05/1990`, as AC-25 needs.

    - I added an exported `dateDigits()` helper.
  - **F01, `shared/date-field.ts`:** the input handler uses `inputType`. When
  Backspace or Delete removes only a `/`, it removes the neighbouring digit
  instead. Backspace right after a `/` removes the digit before the `/`.
  - **F01, `maxlength`:** I kept `maxlength="10"` in `date-field.html`, because
  the new test asserts it. It does not block re-typing, because the mask never
  leaves more than 10 characters.
  - **F02, `shared/input-profile.ts`:** the sanitiser does nothing while
  `event.isComposing` is true or between `compositionstart` and
  `compositionend`. On `compositionend` it sanitises once and dispatches an
  `input` event so the model gets the cleaned value.
  - **F02, date field:** `date-field.ts` skips the mask while composing.

  PNG encoder in that script, because Chromium screenshots come out as RGBA and

  **Spec ambiguities and notes**
  1. **AC-31 and `xmlns`.** AC-31 says the SVG has no "http" or "//" reference.
  A standalone SVG needs `xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"` to render, and the
  implementation has it. I read the rule as "no external reference" and strip
  the `xmlns` declaration before checking. If you want the literal reading, the
  SVG could not render. The spec-writer should clarify this wording.
  2. **Contrast backdrop names.** The spec does not name the composite backdrops
  in `contrast-pairs.json`. I defined `header-bg-over-page-lightest` and
  `header-bg-over-ink-50`, and the frontend-developer used the same names.
  3. **Edge painter.** The spec does not say which element paints the 1px edge.
  The e2e accepts any element, pseudo-element or border-image of the header
  whose computed gradient equals the resolved `--gradient-header-edge` and is
  1px tall.
  4. **Edge token and accent scope.** `--gradient-header-edge` reads
  `--color-country-accent` where it is declared. The implementation redeclares
  it under `[data-country-accent]`, and the e2e confirms the accent shows up.
  Anyone changing this must keep that redeclaration.
